10336-a-select-collection-of-old-english:
This seventh volume of Dodsley's old English plays, in its 1876 fourth edition, gathers five Tudor and Stuart dramas with full notes. Robert Dodsley first issued the collection in 1744; later editors arranged it by date and added notes from all commentators. The plays span tragedy, comedy, and romance from the early English stage.

Tancred and Gismunda, The Wounds of Civil War, Mucedorus, The Two Angry Women of Abington, and Look About You make up the set. Notes trace texts, sources, and stage history for students and readers. The volume offers a rich, scholarly doorway into drama before Shakespeare's age and just after it.
17037-history-of-the-english-people-volu:
John Richard Green's first volume of his History of the English People covers England from the conquest of Britain in 449 to the Charter age. Book One follows early England and the kingdoms, Wessex, and the Northmen. Book Two covers foreign kings from the Conqueror to the Angevins, and Book Three opens with John and the road to the Charter.

Green, a fellow of Jesus College, Oxford, wrote for general readers, with maps and lists of sources for each book. His narrative moves at a brisk, story-like pace while keeping dates and names clear. Students of English history still turn to Green for a readable frame of the early centuries, from Saxon kings to Norman rule.
20800-london-lectures-of-1907:
Sharp lines divide psychism from true spiritual growth in the London Lectures of 1907. The speaker wants each hearer free to choose which path to unfold within. Clear terms, he says, must come before any wise choice of that kind.

Annie Besant, the famed theosophist, gave lectures of this sort to London crowds. Her talks treat karma, rebirth, and the growth of the soul. Theosophy then drew seekers who found old churches too narrow. These lectures show its appeal in plain form: big claims, calm tones, and a promise that hidden laws can be grasped by study.
2107-history-of-friedrich-ii-of-prussia-:
Carlyle calls Book Seven the fearful shipwreck of the double-marriage project, from February to November 1730, when the plan reached deadlock at Berlin. England sent the excellency Hotham, while rebellious women at court refused Weissenfels and took to sickbeds. Hotham, the English envoy, arrived to find Berlin locked in family quarrel.

The king and crown prince ran to Dresden, and the crisis deepened toward Frederick's attempted flight. Carlyle writes the collapse as high drama, with envoys, family rows, and a father's wrath driving the story. The shipwreck metaphor fits, since a plan built on two marriages sank on pride and suspicion.
22905-punch-or-the-london-charivari-vol-:
Punch looks back thirty thousand years in its issue of April 7, 1920, from volume 158. A weekly journal reports, the magazine notes, that the seas around England then stood at a higher level than at present. Nothing much can be done about the matter now, Punch concedes, but it deserves a mention all the same.

That deadpan manner fills the whole number. Jokes, verses, cartoons, and mock reports treat postwar Britain with weary good humor. The Great War had ended, and the magazine's readers were learning peacetime again. A single issue preserves that mood in amber. It also shows Punch's long-lived formula, topical, tidy, and determined to find the small absurdity in every large event.
23056-the-rendezvous-1907:
Ivan Turgenev paints a birch grove in The Rendezvous, his sketch dated 1907 in this translation. Birch leaves in the grove still hold their green, though it has paled with the season. Here and there stood a solitary young birch, all red or all golden. One should have seen how brightly these flushed in the sun, its rays gliding through branches washed by sparkling rain.

Inside that shining wood, a hunter waits and watches a meeting he was never meant to see. A peasant girl and a valet from the great house keep the rendezvous of the title, and class speaks in every gesture. The piece comes from Turgenev's Sportsman's Sketches, the book that quietly indicted serfdom. Nature gets the poetry, people get the truth.
23216-sac-au-dos-1907:
Joris-Karl Huysmans wrote Sac au Dos, a story of the war with Prussia, presented here in a 1907 edition. Its narrator admits he never understood why that butchery of armies was needed. He felt no call to kill others, and none to be killed by them.

Still, he is enrolled in the Seine's Garde Mobile and follows orders. He hunts up an outfit, visits the barber, and reports by seven in the evening to barracks on the Rue Lourcine. Huysmans tells war from inside one reluctant conscript, where duty is routine and the reasons for fighting stay blank.
23219-putois-1907:
Anatole France's Putois, presented in a 1907 edition, is a family tale passed down with care. A parent hands the story on so it will not die with the older generation. The teller's grandfather, Eloi Bergeret, was a man not amused by trifles, yet he set a high value on this piece.

Bergeret called it the Anatomy of Putois, after its central figure. He even said he preferred that anatomy, in some respects, to the anatomy of Quaresmeprenant, a giant from older French tales. France wraps a small household legend in mock learning, and lets family pride do much of the storytelling.
23222-the-fe-te-at-coqueville-1907:
Émile Zola's The Fête at Coqueville, presented in a 1907 edition, tells of a small coastal village and the family that founded it. Coqueville began with the Mahés. That family settled there and grew strong at the foot of the cliff. For a long time, they prospered.

The Mahés married among themselves for centuries, so that the village holds none but Mahés. Then, under Louis XIII, a man named Floche appeared. No one knew much about where he came from. Zola sets a closed, inbred village against one outsider, and lets that contrast drive the fête-day tale.
27562-the-great-events-by-famous-histori:
Rossiter Johnson edited this seventh volume of The Great Events by Famous Historians, published by the National Alumni in 1905. Charles F. Horne and John Rudd served as associate editors, with a staff of specialists. A painting of Jeanne d'Arc at the coronation of Charles VII at Rheims fronts the volume.

The series presents world history through narratives by eminent historians, arranged chronologically. Brief introductions by specialists connect the celebrated narratives, with indices, bibliographies, and chronologies. Volume seven opens with an outline narrative, then Dante composing the Divina Commedia from 1300 to 1318.
2986-mark-twain-a-biography-volume-iii-p:
Albert Bigelow Paine's third volume of Mark Twain: A Biography, part one, covers 1900 to 1907 and opens with the return of the conqueror. Twain comes home after years abroad, staggering under debt and setting out on a pilgrimage of redemption, only to meet sorrow that stirred worldwide sympathy. Newspapers and the public make a stir over his homecoming seldom granted to a private citizen.

Tributes pour in, including a wheelbarrow load of caricatures of famous men, among them a great many of Twain himself. Twain writes that no tribute pleased him more than the friendship of children. A proposed Mark Twain Association at Hannibal marks his native state's pride. The volume follows an old man in full mental vigor, honored at last.
30807-the-works-of-robert-louis-stevenso:
Held here is volume seven of the Swanston Edition of Robert Louis Stevenson's works, printed in London in 1911. The edition ran to twenty-five volumes, with two thousand and sixty copies printed and two thousand for sale. This volume holds one novel, Prince Otto, in three books: Prince Errant, Of Love and Politics, and a closing book on the fate of the prince and his court.

Prince Otto follows a prince who leaves his court on an adventure, plays at being Haroun-al-Raschid, comforts age and beauty, and lectures on love and marriage with comic seriousness. Behind the jokes lie court plots, a council, and a traveler writing on Grünewald. Readers get a witty romance about a ruler who learns, late, what rule and love truly cost.
3083-original-short-stories-volume-07:
From The False Gems to The Apparition, volume seven runs a gamut of love and greed. The False Gems opens with Monsieur Lantin meeting a young girl at a reception at his department head's house and falling head over heels in love. She is the daughter of a dead provincial tax collector, living in Paris with her mother. Other tales include Fascination, Yvette, A Vendetta, My Twenty-Five Days, The Terror, Legend of Mont St. Michel, Friend Patience, Abandoned, The Maison Tellier, Denis, My Wife, and The Unknown.

A feast scene with salt-marsh lamb tender as cake, cider, red wine, and apple brandy shows Maupassant's Norman appetite. The volume mixes love, greed, and the supernatural with his usual economy.
3345-the-wandering-jew-volume-07:
Eugene Sue's serial reaches Book Seven in this volume, with the East Indian in Paris. Rising, doubts, and the letter follow, with Adrienne and Djalma at the center. The consultation, Mother Bunch's diary, and the diary continued lead to the discovery. The trysting-place of the wolves, the common dwelling-house, and the secret close with revelations.

Three days earlier, Mademoiselle de Cardoville had left Dr Baleinier's care, the opening chapter notes, and the plot moves fast from there. Sue pairs his lovers, Adrienne and the Indian prince Djalma, against the conspiracy that hunts them. Readers will find this volume the serial's romantic heart, where diary evidence and a lovers' meeting turn the long plot.
34146-wilson-s-tales-of-the-borders-and-:
Alexander Leighton revised this seventh volume of Wilson's Tales of the Borders and of Scotland, published in London and Newcastle in 1885 by Walter Scott, with a glossary. Tales run from Judith the Egyptian, or The Fate of the Heir of Riccon, by John Mackay Wilson, through the Droich, the Lykewake by Hugh Miller, and the Penny Wedding. The Amateur Lawyers close that run.

The Professor's Tales, family incidents, and the Poor Scholar open the rest. The Laird of Darnick Tower, a tale of the rebellion, the Cateran of Lochloy, Serjeant's Tales, and John Square's voyage to India complete the set. A Border ballad on Judith opens the volume. The book offers Border lore in history, tradition, and fancy.
3557-memoirs-of-napoleon-bonaparte-volum:
This seventh volume of Bourrienne's memoirs covers Napoleon in 1804, the year he crowned himself emperor. Bourrienne writes as a man who had once sat at Napoleon's desk and now watches power harden into ceremony and police. Court ceremony and new imperial titles dominate the year, and Bourrienne notes how quickly old comrades became courtiers.

The year brings the empire's new titles, its court, and its enemies abroad, as France moves from revolution to monarchy in republican dress. Bourrienne records the shift in tone around Napoleon, from comradeship to command. Readers following the series will find here the hinge between consul and emperor, told by an insider who had begun to fall from favor.
3574-recollections-of-the-private-life-o:
Constant's seventh volume stays close to Napoleon's military household, where the valet worked beside aides, orderlies, and guards. He describes headquarters life: maps spread on tables, couriers arriving through the night, and the emperor dictating orders before dawn. The household on campaign was a small, mobile court, and Constant kept it fed, dressed, and ready.

The volume shows the strain of command from the servant's side. Napoleon appears tireless and irritable by turns, kind to old servants and sharp with newcomers. Constant's loyalty gives the account warmth, even when the news is bad. Readers who want war from the antechamber will find a fresh angle here.
3587-essays-of-michel-de-montaigne-volum:
This seventh volume of Montaigne's Essays gathers chapters thirty nine through forty seven of Book One. They include a consideration upon Cicero and the claim that our relish of good and evil depends largely on opinion. Other essays treat honor, inequality among men, sumptuary laws, sleep, the battle of Dreux, names, and the uncertainty of our judgment.

Montaigne moves freely between Roman history, French politics, and his own body and habits. A chapter on sleep sits beside one on a battle, and both serve his main question: how much can we trust our own minds. The volume suits readers who enjoy Montaigne's digressive style and his habit of testing grand ideas against small, daily facts.
3907-the-confessions-of-jean-jacques-rou:
Jean Jacques Rousseau resumes his pen in the seventh book after two years of silence and patience, asking readers to suspend judgment until they have read him. His peaceful youth passed calmly, thanks to an ardent yet feeble nature. Prompt to quit repose for agitation and quick to return from lassitude, he was born for an idle and tranquil state far from great virtues and still further from great vices. Fate, which forced his inclinations for thirty years, then opposed them for thirty more.

Venice supplies the sharpest scenes, as secretary to an ambassador whose house holds no supportable corner, with one filthy candle, pewter plates, and iron forks, and a gondola denied him. The ambassador does not sup, and the staff eats apart in paltry style. Readers who like Rousseau's quarrels will find the Venetian years a study in humiliation and pride.
5281-tales-and-novels-of-j-de-la-fontain:
La Fontaine's seventh volume of tales pairs The Falcon with The Little Dog, opening with a reflection on lovers. The author recalls blaming the avaricious lover, then argues by opposites that the liberal lover should dwell in paradise, and appeals to the Church to prove the rule.

In Florence, a gentle youth loves a beauteous belle with truth, and the falcon of the title becomes the test of his generosity. Readers get two tales in which love is measured by giving, told in verse that turns a lover's sacrifice into both comedy and moral.
5362-the-inside-of-the-cup-volume-07:
Winston Churchill's Inside of the Cup continues in its seventh volume with chapters on the choice, the vestry meeting, Rise, Crowned with Light, and the current of life. It opens with rector John Hodder pondering Alison's note and recalling phrases from Harnack's History of Dogma, around which he frames his reply on faith.

This volume holds only this late portion of the novel, in which Hodder must choose his course before his vestry and congregation. Readers following the story in order will find theology, conscience, and parish politics converging, as Hodder's mission reaches its decisive hour.
5371-richard-carvel-volume-07:
Winston Churchill's Richard Carvel continues in its seventh volume with chapters forty-two through forty-nine. They are My Friends Are Proven, Annapolis Once More, Noblesse Oblige, and The House of Memories. Gordon's Pride, Visitors, Multum in Parvo, and Liberty Loses a Friend follow. It opens at Richard's lodgings, where Banks, red with indignation, reports that Richard's agent has been in possession of his rooms since noon.

Mr Dix lounges in the chair Dolly had chosen, and Richard must reclaim his own. This volume holds only this homeward portion, in which friends are proven and Annapolis is revisited. Liberty itself loses a friend, before the final volume brings Richard home.
5380-a-modern-chronicle-volume-07:
Winston Churchill's Modern Chronicle continues in its seventh volume with a chapter in which it is all done over again. All morning Honora gazes on the shining reaches of the Hudson, deepening to blue as she nears the sea. A gold-bound volume of Shelley lies in her lap, and she repeats two lines that hold a vision of a man terrible and lovely as a tempest.

She summons him out of the chaos of the past. The past becomes the present, as he stands before her in the flesh, his voice and laugh recalled. This volume holds only this late portion of Honora's story, in which memory and reunion test everything she has chosen.
5394-the-crisis-volume-07:
Winston Churchill's Crisis continues in its seventh volume with chapter seven, With the Armies of the West. The scene is Memphis, where the Christmas season approaches, though war recognises no Christmas, Sunday, or holiday, and the brown river, excited by rains, whirls seaward between banks of yellow clay.

Memphis has never seen such activity, possessed by a restless spirit called William T. Sherman, who prods the city and lays violent hold of her. This volume holds only this late wartime portion of the novel, following Stephen and the armies of the West through a Memphis winter of war.
5415-the-memoirs-of-count-grammont-volum:
Anthony Hamilton's memoirs of Philibert de Grammont, edited with notes by Sir Walter Scott, reach a turning point in this seventh volume. The Chevalier de Grammont returns to France, is sent back to England, and watches many of his companions settle into marriage. Court life on both sides of the Channel frames the action.

Grammont's reflections on leaving England give the volume its tone: regret, affection for old friends, and amusement at court ceremony. The chapters gather love intrigues and weddings among the memoir's main figures, closing several long-running stories. It suits readers who enjoy court gossip told by a participant with a sharp eye.
5445-uarda-a-romance-of-ancient-egypt-vo:
Georg Ebers reaches a somber stretch of his ancient Egyptian romance Uarda in this seventh volume. A pioneer's boat finally gets away. It carries his mother and the body of a dog, bound for embalming at Kynopolis, where the dog was held sacred above all animals. Ebers notes that Anubis was the chief divinity worshipped there.

The scene shows how deeply animal worship and burial custom ran through Egyptian life, even in a traveler's private grief. A quarrel between Kynopolis and neighboring Oxyrynchos, where a fish was sacred, underlines the point. Readers get historical romance at its most Egyptian: religion, custom, and daily feeling woven together.
5456-an-egyptian-princess-volume-07:
Georg Ebers sets this seventh volume of An Egyptian Princess in Babylon, where news has filled the whole city before midday. Streets swarm with people waiting to watch a strange spectacle: the punishment of one of the king's wives, proved false and faithless. Whip-bearers struggle to keep the crowds in order as the event approaches.

The volume turns on court justice, royal honor, and public spectacle in the ancient Persian capital. Ebers builds tension from the waiting crowd as much as from the palace itself. Readers get a dramatic, unsettling stretch of historical romance, showing how power displayed itself in Babylon.
5479-cleopatra-volume-07:
Charmian walks toward her own apartments in the seventh volume of Georg Ebers's Cleopatra, turning over a familiar experience. She admires the queen's depth of feeling, strength of intellect, tireless industry, care for her native land, loyalty, and maternal devotion. Then, as before, she is sobered to see Cleopatra pursue a childish purpose at great cost.

The volume shows the queen through her attendant's eyes, balancing admiration with worry. Ebers lets Charmian's mixed feelings carry the portrait. Readers get an intimate, conflicted view of Cleopatra, where greatness and fault sit side by side in one household.
5489-the-emperor-volume-07:
While Pollux and his grieving mother wait for Euphorion's return in the seventh volume of Georg Ebers's The Emperor, Papias flatters the emperor. He pretends that Hadrian is merely Claudius Venator, the architect. Meanwhile Aurelius Verus, nicknamed by Alexandrians the sham Eros, lives through strange experiences, visiting the empress in the afternoon in hope of some favor.

The volume weaves waiting, flattery, and court visits through Hadrian's Alexandria, where identity and favor are traded daily. Ebers keeps several households in motion at once. Readers get a busy, ironic stretch of the romance, where everyone plays a part before the emperor.
5514-arachne-volume-07:
Without a word of explanation, Hermon drags his guide along in breathless haste in the seventh volume of Georg Ebers's Arachne. No one stops them. The atrium, usually swarming with guards, servants, and officials until late, stands completely deserted as the blind man hurries through with his friend. The door to the outer air stands open.

The volume turns on flight and urgency, as a blind sculptor escapes a guarded house with only a scholar's arm to guide him. Ebers keeps the scene taut and visual despite its hero's blindness. Readers get a suspenseful stretch of the romance, where an open door means freedom or danger.
5523-the-bride-of-the-nile-volume-07:
If Philippus found no sleep that night, neither did Orion in the seventh volume of Georg Ebers's The Bride of the Nile. Orion no longer doubts Paula, but his heart longs to hear her say once more that she loves him and him alone, and yearning keeps him awake. He springs from bed at dawn's first glimmer, glad the night is past.

The volume follows sleepless lovers toward morning, with longing rather than action driving the hours. Ebers keeps the romance intimate, in bedrooms and first light. Readers get a tender, restless stretch of the story, where a single hoped-for sentence matters most.
5536-a-thorny-path-volume-07:
The high priest of Serapis presides over sacrifices this morning in the seventh volume of Georg Ebers's A Thorny Path. Caesar has given beasts in abundance to honor the god, yet the priest goes ill-disposed to his part. An imperial command has filled citizens' houses with troops, authorized to make unheard-of demands on their hosts, and that order has roused his anger against the ruler.

The volume sets temple ritual against military occupation in Alexandria, with a priest's resentment sharpening the scene. Ebers shows how imperial power pressed on household and shrine alike. Readers get a tense, political stretch of the romance, where sacrifice proceeds under protest.
5558-margery-gred-a-tale-of-old-nurember:
My Uncle Christian growls a threat out near the stables in the seventh volume of Georg Ebers's Margery, a tale of old Nuremberg. Meanwhile Matthew puts the bridle on Margery's bay nag, and serving men saddle horses for the gentlemen. Margery has stolen there, knowing the old folks would not have let her ride forth after Ann. Her uncle's grumbling about the old owl shows a household on the move.

The volume follows a headstrong girl slipping out to follow her kin, with horses, uncles, and household scolding in play. Ebers writes the scene in Margery's lively voice. Readers get a spirited stretch of the tale, where a stolen ride promises adventure.
5567-barbara-blomberg-volume-07:
Through a storm lashing her face with dust and rain, Barbara reaches the little Prebrunn castle in the seventh volume of Georg Ebers's Barbara Blomberg. The marquise has not yet left her litter, wind has blown out two torches, and one bearer walks ahead with his flame blown aside. Before Barbara reaches the gate, a man hidden behind the old elm by the path steps forward.

The volume turns on a stormy arrival and a concealed figure waiting by the gate. Ebers writes weather and suspense together. Readers get a dramatic stretch of the romance, where a castle gate becomes a place of confrontation.
5788-a-tramp-abroad-volume-07:
Volume seven of Mark Twain's A Tramp Abroad covers chapters forty-three through fifty, from Chamonix to Rome and Florence. Chapters treat contrasts at Chamonix and the guild of guides. A rigid record book and the conqueror of Mont Blanc follow. Later pages look at Mont Blanc by telescope, a catastrophe that cost eleven lives, the Glacier des Bossons, and Geneva shops with elastic prices. Milan, Venice, and Saint Mark's follow.

The trip with Twain from Alpine guides to Italian art, hearing him weigh what is grand, what is humbug, and what endures. The closing chapters ask why some things are, treating art in Rome and Florence with Twain's mix of awe and irreverence. This final volume gathers the tramp's themes, as Europe's beauty and its tourist traps meet in one comic verdict.
5909-the-history-of-don-quixote-volume-1:
Sancho limps back to his master in chapter eighteen of this Don Quixote installment, so faint he cannot urge his beast onward. Don Quixote, seeing his state, draws a conclusion about their hardships, and the discourse that follows fills chapter eighteen with adventures worth relating. Chapter nineteen continues their shrewd talk, chapter twenty brings an unexampled adventure, and chapter twenty-one treats Mambrino's helmet as an exalted prize.

Chapter twenty-two closes the installment with freedom conferred on several unfortunates against their will, in Quixote's chivalric logic. Readers get Quixote and Sancho at their most argumentative, as squire's sense meets master's madness. The part suits readers following the knight in order, since its jokes about helmets, freedom, and discourse echo through later chapters.
72276-the-taylor-trotwood-magazine-vol-i:
This number of a monthly sheet was printed at Nashville, Tennessee, for February 1907. Governor Bob Taylor and John Trotwood Moore are named as its heads. The sheet costs a dime a copy, or a coin of one weight for a year. The list of parts shows a mix of tale, verse, and fact. A piece on the Jamestown fair, with cuts, stands at the head, by James Hines.

A poem comes next, then a life of General Joseph E. Johnston by Robert L. Taylor, with cuts. Young folk of the South have a piece of their own. A long run of parts on the great roads of the South and on the past of one clan fills the mid pages. A story of how old Wash played Santa Claus stands by a tale of love.
7592-the-caxtons-a-family-picture-volume:
Part seven of The Caxtons is Lytton at his most playful, turning family speculation into comedy. Its warning comes from Luther's Table Talk, where a doctor who counts his hanging puddings is told he will not live long. The narrator wishes he had set that passage before his father at breakfast, in large round hand, on the morning before a fatal evening. Uncle Jack then persuaded the father to count his own puddings.

Uncle Jack's philosophy explains the joke. The narrator doubts he knew much of Democritus of Abdera, yet calls him tainted by that fanciful sage's thought, which filled the air with huge images that shaped dreams and divinations. Schemes fill the air the same way here. The part laughs at speculation pursued until it becomes absurd.
7621-pelham-volume-07:
Pelham reflects on party loyalty in this part, and the reflection turns from dandyism to conscience. He did not embrace his party from any private or interested motive, he insists, and therefore no private motive justifies deserting it. Honor, once chosen, must be kept when it costs most. The part weighs honor against advantage in the world of politics, and finds advantage wanting.

The faction he defends is praised in high terms. The Dawton faction holds the best, the purest, and the wisest of the day. Lord Dawton is merely the channel through which their measures flow. The narrator rises early, calmed by sleep, to think his position over. That quiet morning, not a speech or a bargain, settles his course. Loyalty here is a morning decision, not a performance.
7637-the-disowned-volume-07:
Near the close of Edward Bulwer Lytton's novel The Disowned, this seventh volume turns on a rival claim for Lady Flora's hand. Lord Ulswater asks for one meeting at noon, promising to step aside if he cannot prove his rival false. Letters, family pressure, and old secrets drive the action forward.

Flora must weigh duty against her own hopes while her mother tries to buy time for calm thought. The volume also follows Wolfe and Mr. Brown on the road, where a sharp exchange softens into a plain apology. Pride, rank, and love clash here, and the ending of the long plot starts to come into view.
7646-ernest-maltravers-volume-07:
Lumley Ferrers takes center stage in Book Seven of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Ernest Maltravers. From boyhood he has lived by a cold plan: enjoy youth, chase gain, and let others pay the cost. Now grown, he works his way through travel, talk, and useful friends with the same cool method.

The volume follows his push toward office and power, including a hard-fought election and praise in the party press. Around him, Maltravers and his circle face the price of such schemes. The book asks how far charm and planning can carry a man who feels little for anyone else.
7656-kenelm-chillingly-volume-07:
Tom Bowles arrives unannounced at Kenelm's lodgings in Book Seven of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Kenelm Chillingly, to a frugal supper and frank talk. Kenelm urges plain dealing: Tom should come to the Somers hearth as a true friend, not a man with a secret to hide.

A tale told within the volume, of a prince whose deforming frame is cut free so that white wings may grow, mirrors the theme of change through pain. Love, pride, and honest friendship run through these chapters, as Kenelm presses his friend toward a more open and steady course.
7665-what-will-he-do-with-it-volume-07:
Darrell praises Honoria Vipont with sly wit in Book Seven of Edward Bulwer Lytton's What Will He Do With It? He calls her rational, prudent, and free of romance, a heroine out of Maria Edgeworth who would marry with dignity and lose a husband with decorum. Alban takes the jest as praise.

The volume then follows Matilda Darrell's schooling in drawing, languages, and science, which leaves her mind and temper unchanged. Through talk of books and young ladies' learning, the book mocks neat plans for shaping character while real feeling goes its own way.
7678-harold-the-last-of-the-saxon-kings-:
Sunset over the Conway river opens Book Seven of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Harold, subtitled The Welch King. A rude fort above the Gyffin and ruins of a Roman town frame a brave Welsh prince who waits his doom among stones older than any northern crown.

A Norman observer sees only old wreckage where the Welsh see heroic lineage. Later the tale turns to a vast oval barrow of loose stones, ringed by stone walls whose date even bards cannot name. War, pride, and the weight of ruined empires hang over this volume.
7698-a-strange-story-volume-07:
Lilian's gentle nature survives the loss of reason in the seventh volume of Edward Bulwer Lytton's A Strange Story. She sits calm and silent for hours, murmuring of wanderings with her father as if he still lived, and her drawings grow strange and lovely, like Blake's visions for Night Thoughts.

Calling her back to real life only troubles her eyes and draws heavy sighs. A walk with Julius Faber brings a wild laugh from a she-oak, which he blames on a kingfisher. The volume holds grief, wonder, and a mind seeking refuge in an imagined heaven.
7708-my-novel-volume-07:
Captain Roland asks what courage means in Book Seven of Edward Bulwer Lytton's My Novel, after the family hears the sixth book read aloud. Mr. Caxton admits he faced a rushing bull in fear, not calm, and argues that honor, not blind nerve, makes a man stand his ground.

The volume also carries an exile's plea: cease seeking justice from ministers and kings, lest spies find his track, for he has taught his child to pray for his friend's name. Through talk and letters, it weighs fear, honor, and the price of loyalty to a hunted man.
7721-the-last-of-the-barons-volume-07:
Hastings strides into the White Tower council chamber in Book Seven of Edward Bulwer Lytton's The Last of the Barons, subtitled The Popular Rebellion. Edward stands erect in a tight tunic, no longer lounging in loose robes, with open letters and a dagger on the table before grave lords.

A courier from the north has brought grave news, and the White Lion of March shakes his mane. Later Montagu defends Hilyard, recalling how the rebel once saved him from Lancastrian swords after Hexham. The volume turns a court summons into the spark of a people's rising.
7734-paul-clifford-volume-07:
Lucy's winter drags in the seventh volume of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Paul Clifford, the dreariest season of her life, as judges ride out to visit prisons. The novel mocks a system where legal gentry feast and draw fees from suspense, fear, sentence, and death, turning tears into wine.

Quoting Seneca on fortune's unfair gifts and Goldsmith on an open door for want, the volume follows Lucy through weeks of waiting. Letters bring a cordial hope, like a new lease of life. Law, mercy, and a young woman's endurance stand at the heart of these chapters.
7743-the-parisians-volume-07:
May 1870 finds Gustave Rameau a power in Paris salons in Book Seven of Lytton's The Parisians. His journal gains hold, his share of profits grows, and clique critics praise his verse above Musset in vigor and Hugo in polish, though few common readers actually read it.

Rameau lives up to his income in a fine bachelor's flat, keeps a coupe, and dines well at the Cafe Anglais, following the way of fashionable writers. The volume satirizes literary fame built on mutual praise, where being courted matters more than being read.
7907-american-historical-and-literary-cu: What the text file holds for part seven of Smith and Watson's American Historical and Literary Curiosities is an editor's note and little besides the title. The series, the note says, consists of illustrations and page images, with only a few text passages fit to scan. Readers should open the HTML edition.
8785-the-divine-comedy-by-dante-illustra:
This seventh part of Dante's Inferno, in Cary's translation, covers cantos eighteen through twenty-two, deep in Malebolge, the evil pouches. A place of dark-stained rock, ringed like a castle's moat, holds ten trenches in its hollow bottom, where fraud in its many forms is punished. Panders, seducers, flatterers, simonists, soothsayers, and barrators appear in turn, each trench with its own filth or fire.

Canto eighteen's comparison of Malebolge's fosses to castle defences shows Dante's architectural imagination at work. Later cantos bring demons, boiling pitch, and the witty, dangerous talk of the barrators. The part is among the Inferno's most inventive, and its punishments, tailored to each fraud, repay slow reading. Readers meet Dante the satirist here, as much as Dante the theologian.
9769-alice-or-the-mysteries-book-07:
Book seven of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Alice, or The Mysteries, opens as Lord Vargrave dons his greatcoat to visit Lisle Court. Lord Saxingham enters, surprised at a country trip, and notes Vargrave will pass near C-----. Vargrave jokes that he knows Poland, Mexico, and Madagascar inch by inch, yet never learned England's geography at school. His carriage waits at the door.

The book follows Vargrave's country errand, where dark words breed suspicion. Lytton's prose favors intrigue and polished talk. A reader gets the seventh book of a Victorian mystery romance, where a statesman's journey hides a deeper design.
a-modern-chronicle-volume-07:
Winston Churchill's A Modern Chronicle, volume seven, carries Book Three from chapter eleven, In Which It Is All Done Over Again. Honora's life has repeated its pattern: a new attachment, a new world. The Entrance into Eden brings her by night train to Hugh Chiltern's country. A Gothic station ends the line, on Chiltern's own railway.

Chiltern, like a schoolboy, shows her the feudal domain where his family has ruled. Of the World Beyond the Gates and Philosophy from Mr. Grainger widen the view. The Pillars of Society closes the volume, naming the forces Honora must satisfy or defy. Churchill is writing the divorce-era novel of manners at full stretch: a woman twice bound, a lover with a principality, and society's pillars watching. Eden, in his irony, has a station, a timetable, and neighbours who will talk.
a-select-collection-of-old-english-plays: Robert Dodsley continues his select collection of old English plays in this seventh volume, with notes by W. Carew Hazlitt. Its plays range from the tragedy of Tancred and Gismunda and the wounds of civil war to the comedy Mucedorus, two angry women of Abington, and a look about you. Tancred and Gismund, compiled by gentlemen of the Inner Temple and printed in 1591, survives from a 1568 original known only in manuscript, now collated with the printed text.
a-strange-story-volume-07: Edward Bulwer Lytton continues his strange story in this seventh volume with Lilian in the suspension of her reason, her wondrous gentleness unlost. Habitually calm and very silent, she speaks rarely of earthly things, her thought having quitted the earth for some imaginary heaven. She talks of roaming with her father as though he lived still, murmurs in converse with invisible spirits, and quietly resumes drawing and music when unobserved.
a-thorny-path-volume-07:
Volume 7 of A Thorny Path, by Georg Ebers, opens on sacrifice day in Alexandria, with the high priest of Serapis presiding. Ebers shows a city squeezed by imperial orders: troops are billeted, meaning lodged by force, in citizens' houses and told they may demand whatever they like. The priest goes to his duties angry at the tyrant who ordered it, yet half admiring the man's gifts.

Chapter XXI brings word that a state galley has sailed to overtake the ship carrying Melissa's father and brother, and to free them. Melissa breakfasts with the lady Euryale while Philostratus tells the news. Her joy worries her friends, who fear the emperor will want this fresh, lovely girl for himself. Relief and dread arrive in the same hour.
a-tramp-abroad-volume-07:
A Tramp Abroad, Part 7, by Mark Twain, closes the tramp at Chamonix under Mont Blanc and ends the book in Italy. Twain begins with contrasts at the great mountain and a proposed way of looking at it by telescope. Then he turns grave for a chapter: a catastrophe that cost eleven lives, the Mont Blanc accident of 1870, retold from the record.

Geneva's shops and elastic prices restore the comedy, followed by Milan's arcade and Venice, where St Mark's Cathedral prompts one of his set pieces. The final chapter asks why some things are, and tours art in Rome and Florence, fig leaf included. Twain's tramp, who set out to walk Europe, finishes as he lived: riding when he could, joking at guides and glaciers alike, and saving his real awe for mountains and old masters.
a-vanished-arcadia-being-some-account-of:
A Vanished Arcadia, published in 1901 by R B Cunninghame Graham, gives an account of the Jesuits in Paraguay between 1607 and 1767. Graham describes the Christian commonwealth of the Jesuit missions between the Paraná and Uruguay rivers. There the Jesuits built their famous reductions, towns where the Guaraní lived under mission rule, until the order was expelled.

Graham examines whether the work the Jesuits did among the Indians was beneficial, the question that has hung over the missions ever since. His account weighs the protection and order of the reductions against their control and their sudden end. The book, issued with a map, remains a readable English history of that lost world.
abbott-behind-scenes-mediums-1907:
David Abbott lifts the veil on seer craft in Behind the Scenes with the Mediums, his book of 1907. Abbott was a stage mage in Omaha who spent years in dark rooms as a guest. He learned each trick from the in side: slate writes, rope ties that slip, forms made of gauze, and the code talk of mates hid in the crowd of guests.

He prints the whole craft in clear, wry prose. Fans of the faith cursed his name for it. Busters cite the book more than most. It is the best guide to the tricks of its age.
adams-education-henry-adams-1907:
Henry Adams, grandson and great-grandson of American presidents, wrote his life story in the third person, as if watching a student fail. First printed in a small private edition in 1907, the book reached the public after his death. It is now counted among the great American life stories.

Adams says his schooling left him unready for a world of banks, machines, and raw power. His famous chapters set the Virgin of the old cathedrals against the dynamo of the new factories. That contrast still frames how readers think about faith, force, and modern life.
alchemy-and-the-alchemists-giving-the-se:
Alchemy and the Alchemists, published in 1907 by R Swinburne Clymer, argues a bold thesis about the old art. Its full title promises the secret of the philosopher's stone, the elixir of youth, and the universal solvent. It then claims that the true alchemists did not seek to transmute base metals into gold at all, but sought the highest initiation, the development of the spiritual nature in man.

Clymer reads the furnaces and metals of the alchemical books as symbols of an inner work. On his account, knowing the stone means knowing oneself, and the gold is a perfected human nature. The book belongs to the occult revival of its decade, and it preserves that movement's spiritual reading of alchemy in full.
alice-or-the-mysteries-book-07: Edward Bulwer Lytton returns to Lord Vargrave in the seventh book of Alice, or the Mysteries, as his travelling carriage waits and Lord Saxingham calls about Lisle Court. Talk of counties, journeys, and forgotten geography masks the peer's designs on estates and marriage. The book moves the plot toward the country houses where its fortunes will be settled.
american-historical-and-literary-curiosi: John Jay Smith's seventh part of American Historical and Literary Curiosities adds more plates to the series. The editor's note is frank: the book is pictures and page images, so this text holds few readable passages, and the HTML file is urged instead. For readers, the plates remain the point, keeping the look of old papers.
an-egyptian-princess-volume-07:
Georg Ebers's An Egyptian Princess, volume seven, in Eleanor Grove's translation, opens as news of royal doings spreads before midday. A sharp-witted Athenian reads the sad story clearly, in the second chapter's phrase. Prexaspes, the king's messenger and one of Persia's highest officials, carries Cambyses' orders. The court of the conqueror is becoming a court of fear.

Cambyses' reign darkens in these chapters toward the crimes Herodotus recorded: a brother marked for death, a court governed by suspicion. Prexaspes, forced to execute his master's secret commands, embodies the tyranny's machinery. Ebers follows his Greek sources while filling their silences with Egyptian and Persian colour. Grove's version keeps the narrative's operatic sweep. Volume seven belongs to the king's unravelling, watched by Greeks who will write the history. The Athenian's clear sight is the reader's: a great empire rotting at its head.
arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-07:
Volume seven of the Thousand Nights and a Night, in Burton's translation of 1885, continues the great cycle. Shahrazad's tales by now fill years of nights, and the king has children by his storyteller. The frame's danger has cooled into habit, wonder, and a kind of education for the throne.

Burton keeps his method steady: literal text, full verse, and notes that range from grammar to geography. Sailors, slaves, caliphs, and demons share the stage in turn. The Arabic book had grown for centuries by accretion, and Burton honors that layered growth. Readers step in anywhere, yet the long arc rewards those who persist. Volume seven is deep water, well stocked.
arachne-volume-07:
Volume 7 of Arachne, by Georg Ebers, opens with an arrest that neither prisoner can explain. Ebers brings the blind sculptor Hermon out of a palace banquet, leaning on his friend Crates, a scholar of the Museum. The outer door stands open, the atrium lies empty, and armed Macedonian soldiers wait in the courtyard beyond the plants.

Chapter VIII gives the seizure in the king's name, with a warning to stay silent on pain of death. Hermon names himself and his friend, certain some mistake has been made. The officer only asks whether they came from Proclus's banquet, then orders both men chained. Numbers and royal orders leave no room for protest. A night of honor ends in irons, and the charge stays unspoken.
arxiv-2412-01507:
Eskin, Korobov, Martynenko, and Martynenko compute the resonant states of muonic three-particle systems pairing a negative muon with light nuclei. Their paper from twenty twenty-four covers four combinations: helium with protons or deuterons, lithium with protons or deuterons. A variational approach with exponential and Gaussian basis sets carries the calculation. Resonances, the short-lived states above breakup thresholds, are the quarry.

Complex coordinate rotation exposes those states as clean eigenvalues of the rotated problem. The method turns decaying resonances into stationary targets that variational machinery can hit. Muonic molecules matter because the heavy muon squeezes nuclei close enough to interest fusion and precision spectroscopy alike. The energy tables give both fields fresh reference values for these exotic three-body systems.
arxiv-2412-05807:
David Woodruff and Samson Zhou improve ways to track the most frequent items in a stream of data when a foe can shape the stream as it comes. Their paper is from two thousand twenty-four.

In such streams, the goal is to sum up a huge set while using far less space than the set's size. A past trick joined sparse recovery with tools from privacy work to stay sound against a foe. The team first builds a better tracker for the top items, with sound trade-offs. They then use it to cut the task down to a gauge of the tail of the stream. A new tool for that gauge, in the plain stream case, rounds out the work.
arxiv-2412-07707:
Giovanni Battista Carollo, Massimiliano Semeraro, Giuseppe Gonnella, and Marco Zamparo compute rare work surges on a trapped Brownian particle. Their paper, from twenty twenty-four, studies a particle in a harmonic well. A random force does work on it, and big deviations from the average are the quarry. The team derives the rate function for general starting spreads.

Depending on the initial spread, the curve shows zero, one, or two kinks. Each kink marks where straight-line tails switch on. Wide starts tie the pattern to the well's strength. Stationary starts give one kink; tight starts give none. A big early jump explains the kinks' origin. Simulations confirm the math.
arxiv-2412-10207:
Xiao Zhang, Qianru Meng, and Johan Bos teach language models to turn sentences into formal meaning maps with help from a fetched word store. Their paper appeared in two thousand twenty-four. Semantic parsing maps plain text into a strict form that machines can reason over. Neural parsers often trip on words and ideas they never saw in training.

Their method, RASP, pulls in outside symbolic knowledge about words during parsing. Large language models already beat older encoder-decoder parsers on the task. Adding the fetched knowledge nearly doubled scores on concepts outside the training data. That gain shows the models use the store rather than just their memory. The authors argue that pairing big models with lookup tools is a strong path. It points toward parsers that hold up in open, shifting domains.
arxiv-2412-10907:
Antonino D'Aì and a large team of co-authors studied the X-ray pulsar V 0332+53 in twenty twenty-four, hunting for wings on its cyclotron absorption line. This accreting neutron star's spectrum carries a line carved by electrons spiraling in its immense magnetic field. Using all available NuSTAR observations, the team built energy-resolved pulse profiles and pulsed fraction spectra with a tailored pipeline.

Where statistics were strong, two symmetric bump features flanked the line's energy, barely moving as the source brightened. The authors interpret them as the line's resonant absorption wings, as theory predicts for the line shape along our line of sight. Phase-resolved analysis around the features let them separate the spectral shape of the line-forming region from the rest of the emission.
arxiv-2412-13707:
The CONUS Collaboration measures the background radiation at the site of its new neutrino experiment in Switzerland, in a paper published in two thousand twenty-four. The experiment, CONUS+, hunts for a subtle effect: reactor antineutrinos bouncing off whole germanium nuclei at once, a process called coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering.

The detector sits about twenty-one meters from the core of the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, where the antineutrino flux is intense. Four high-purity germanium detectors with very low energy thresholds will record the tiny recoils. Success depends on knowing every other source of counts in that hall. Background events that track the reactor's heat output are especially troublesome, since they can mimic the signal's rhythm. The paper characterizes that environment before the main run. It continues a program begun at a German plant. Careful background work is what lets a faint neutrino signal stand out.
arxiv-2412-15707:
Martin Bichler, Julius Durmann, and Matthias Oberlechner ask whether pricing algorithms collude, testing bandit learners in repeated Bertrand competition. Their paper from twenty twenty-four speaks to regulators watching algorithmic pricing spread through digital markets. Bandit algorithms are apt suspects: they learn from little information, much like real automated pricers. The analysis shows mean-based learners converge to correlated rationalizable actions.

In Bertrand settings that means Nash equilibrium prices, or neighbors of them. Numerical runs find most bandit variants converging likewise. Supra-competitive prices appear only when every seller runs the same symmetric algorithm, a certain upper-confidence-bound flavor, and the effect fades as competitors multiply. Mixed algorithm populations look reassuringly competitive. The collusion fear, in this stylized market, needs sameness to bite.
arxiv-2412-16707:
Dharmaraj Ramachandran and Radhika Vathsan argue that the standard shape-based gauge of quantum entanglement is too blunt. Their paper appeared in twenty twenty-four. Two states that no local unitary can turn into each other can still get the same gauge score. The pair use the success rate of teleport steps to show why that blunt score misleads.

They fix the gauge by a small change to its base rule and call the new form the Sharp Geometric Measure. Math shows the same score can be reached from two shape views of state space. A new gauge for true multi-part links builds on it. The new tools fix two known flaws of past gauges.
arxiv-2501-12307:
Ramesh Prasad Panda and Papi Ray wrote this math paper in two thousand twenty-five. It sorts the finite groups whose order supergraphs can be split by a cyclic vertex cutset, a set of points whose removal breaks the graph into parts that each hold a cycle.

The order supergraph of a group links two elements when the order of one divides the order of the other. The authors pin down the nilpotent groups with this split trait. They then do the same for named non-nilpotent families: dihedral, dicyclic, EPPO, symmetric, and alternating groups. The paper is a piece of algebraic graph theory.
arxiv-2501-14907:
Ivan Bocanegra-Garay, L. Hernández-Sánchez, and H. Moya-Cessa used supersymmetry as a master key for quantum optics models in a 2025 paper. Cavity quantum electrodynamics studies atoms exchanging photons inside resonators, and its counter-rotating contact terms, usually discarded as small, create motion that resist exact analysis. The authors map the counter-rotating problem onto its rotating counterpart through a supersymmetric transformation. Making an otherwise intractable contact fully and exactly analyzable in general.

Traits hidden in the counter-rotating system become visible through the simple map. The method is applied to a curved Kerr-like model and to linear multiphoton Jaynes–Cummings models. Supersymmetry, borrowed from high-energy theory, emerges here as a useful tool for connecting and constructing exactly solvable photonic systems with possible device applications.
arxiv-2502-02407:
Sidak Pal Singh, Hossein Mobahi, Atish Agarwala, and Yann Dauphin diagnose why a popular training trick helps vision models but hurts language models, in a paper published in two thousand twenty-five. The trick is sharpness-aware minimization, which steers training toward flat valleys in the loss landscape that tend to generalize better.

In language tasks the method often degrades results, even when given double the compute. The authors trace the failure to a side channel: the algorithm ends up regularizing the statistics of the model's output scores rather than the function's geometry. That logit manipulation is spurious minimization, motion that looks like progress but is not. Their fix, Functional-SAM, regularizes curvature only through the overall function's statistics. Preconditioning the perturbation step helps too, and together the two broaden where sharpness methods work.
arxiv-2502-09307:
Samuel Amouyal, Aya Meltzer-Asscher, and Jonathan Berant compare readers in twenty twenty-five. Garden-path sentences mislead readers into a wrong parse, then force a re-read. Humans find them notoriously hard. The authors ask whether large language models stumble in the same places, and for the same reasons.

They turn psycholinguistic hypotheses into tests. Human participants and a large suite of models answered comprehension questions on garden-path items. Both groups struggled with specific syntactic complexities. Some models correlated strongly with human comprehension patterns. Paraphrase and image generation tasks gave matching results. Readers see where machine parsing mirrors human parsing, and where the resemblance breaks. The study treats models as subjects in a classic language experiment.
arxiv-2502-11907:
Andrew Zheng, Spyros Alexakis, and Adam Stinchcombe give new ways to compute hard sums over smooth surfaces, where the term blows up or near blows up. Their paper is from two thousand twenty-five.

Such sums rule a class of equations for waves and flow. When a surface is cut into flat triangles, a mild blow-up turns strong. Past tricks work for the base kernel but fail for its slope across the surface, which blows up more. The team gives forms for both the kernel and its slope on smooth faces, for many known operators. For the slope case, they set out a fresh geometric path and closed forms.
arxiv-2502-12907:
Daniel Martinez-Gil, Pedro Bargueno, and Salvador Miret-Artes settle which kinds of influence can split the energy of left and right handed chiral systems. The question turns on the split between true and false chirality. Their work came out in twenty twenty-five.

Using mirror molecules as the model case of true chirality, the team proves in a field theory frame that only a truly chiral force can lift the tie. The weak force, carried by the Z boson, is such a force. A falsely chiral force, like an axion based one, cannot do it. The results extend classic ideas on chirality and parity breach.
arxiv-2503-02707:
Tessa Masis and colleagues analyzed the online StopAsianHate movement in 2025. The movement against anti-Asian violence began in 2021 during the COVID-19 period and spread worldwide, yet earlier research covered mainly English-speaking users and short time spans. The team wanted to know how the conversation looked in other languages and over the long term.

They studied millions of tagged tweets from millions of users in sixty languages, mixing topic modeling, user modeling, and hand checking. English and non-English discussions differed clearly in which events drove spikes of activity, and the K-pop fan presence formed part of the movement's reach. The study gives the first long-term, multilingual picture of how the campaign traveled and who kept it going.
arxiv-2503-03207:
Pei-Wei Chen and six co-authors present PolyVer, a way to check software systems built from code in many languages at once. Checkers today are made for one language, so mixed systems are often translated first, which can warp them. Their work came out in twenty twenty-five.

PolyVer models the real system as a state machine whose step rules stay in their home languages, such as C or Rust. A model checker then works with language specific checkers through contracts for each step rule. Those contracts are drafted by synthesis tools or large language models and checked by the home checkers. With these short forms, the checker proves the whole system trait.
arxiv-2503-03507:
Samuel Repka and four co-authors sort minerals in microscope images by fusing two kinds of data. Their paper came out in two thousand twenty-five. Scanning electron microscopes give backscattered electron images of rock samples. Those images alone often lack the detail to name each mineral. Chemical spectra at single points are accurate but slow to gather. Full chemical maps would take far too long.

The team fuses sparse spectra with the full image using graph neural networks. The graph form suits the scattered, uneven layout of point spectra. The network labels each region with its mineral phase. Image texture and chemistry inform each other in the process. Tests show the fusion beats image-only sorting. The method speeds up mineral analysis for geology and mining.
arxiv-2503-03607:
Keqi Chen and five co-authors present Psy-Insight, a data set for mental health counseling in two thousand twenty-five. Language models could aid mental health support through in-context learning. Data for training them is thin, most of all in Chinese. Psy-Insight is billed as the first data set of its kind.

It holds face to face, multi turn counseling talks in two languages. Tags cover therapy type, emotion, strategy, and topic. Each turn has its reasons spelled out, and each session has guidance. Tests show trained models copy style and grasp strategy too. The set can train models to act as kind counselors with clear logic.
arxiv-2503-03707:
Annie Chen, Alec Lessing, Yuejiang Liu, and Chelsea Finn let robots grade their own training data. Their paper, from twenty twenty-five, tackles demo sets of mixed quality. Robot learners copy shown actions, but weak or rare strategies in the data can drag them down. People find it slow and costly to weed those demos out by hand.

Their method, Demo-SCORE, trains a judge from the robot's own trial runs. The judge learns to tell success from failure rollouts. It then filters the demo set before final training. Tests in simulation and on real robots show cleaner policies. Success rates rose by fifteen to thirty-five points over unfiltered training.
arxiv-2503-06707:
Brian Huge and Antoine Savine extend differential machine learning with a supervised twist on principal component analysis. Classic PCA finds the axes of greatest variation in data, blind to what the modeler actually cares about. Their variant chooses axes that matter for a target problem, shrinking derivatives models to their informative core.

Derivatives pricing lives in high dimensions, where every kept dimension costs time. The authors aim the reduction at three concrete jobs. It can specify and calibrate pricing models with fewer, better factors. It can pick regression features for least-squares Monte Carlo, a workhorse of early-exercise pricing. It can also pre-process simulated data sets before differential learning begins. The theme is supervision: let the downstream task, not raw variance, decide which directions deserve to survive.
arxiv-2503-07407:
Keshab Kauchha, Peifan Liu, Paresh Pradhan, and Yuri Shvydko designed a spectrograph for a future kind of X-ray laser that would fire fully coherent pulses from a cavity. Such a source promises very pure colors and a fast pulse rate, but steering it requires measuring each pulse spectrum with fine detail. Writing in twenty twenty-five, the team built an instrument based on bending X-rays off crystals at precise angles. It captures a window of spectrum in a single shot at high brightness, aimed at X-rays near a stated energy.

In tests at a synchrotron beamline, the device spread the spectrum at the designed rate and imaged its window faithfully. Measured sharpness reached about twenty milli-electronvolts, roughly half the design goal, which the team traces to tiny angular wobbles of the crystals. The result still shows a workable diagnostic for the new lasers.
arxiv-2503-08207:
Denan Li and co-authors wrote this perspective paper, published in two thousand twenty-five, on whether universal machine-learned force fields can be trusted for real simulations. These foundation-style models promise quantum accuracy at classical speed for almost any material.

Rather than run a broad benchmark, the authors put the models through one hard test: the heat-driven phase switch in lead titanate, a classic ferroelectric. At zero temperature the models reproduce the basics well. At working temperatures, cracks show: the phase change comes out wrong in places, and some runs go unstable. The authors blame slanted training data and a thin grasp of anharmonic motion. They stress the point is not to rank models. It is to start an honest talk about readiness, and about the fine-tuning that may close the gap.
arxiv-2503-09607:
Fulvio Melia reexamined the mass weighing on a cosmic lens in a 2025 paper. The James Webb telescope found a compact galaxy bending a farther galaxy's light into a complete Einstein ring. Two studies of the system disagreed over whether stars plus ordinary dark matter suffice, or whether extra mass is required, with different inferred distances to the lensed galaxy driving the split. Melia asks whether the background cosmology itself shifts the verdict.

Comparing the standard flat model with his preferred alternative cosmology, he reports the mass shortfall appears in both, and neither is favored by this ring. The gap therefore stays open, pointing, in his reading, to a possible new mass component or a revised stellar mass function in the lens galaxy.
arxiv-2503-11207:
Giacomo Camposampiero and colleagues test whether flagship reasoning models can solve visual analogy puzzles when perception gets unreliable. The puzzles are Raven's progressive matrices, the classic nonverbal IQ format. Two leading reasoning models were benchmarked on a standard set and a harder extension with longer rules and wider value ranges. Writing in twenty twenty-five, the team also corrupted the inputs two ways. Random distractor attributes were added, and attribute distributions were smoothed. Both mimic imperfect eyesight feeding the reasoner.

Accuracy collapsed. One model fell from strong performance to near chance on the harder, noisier set. It burned several times more reasoning tokens while failing. The rival model fell similarly. A neuro-symbolic probabilistic model, by contrast, held up across all the corrupted tests. The authors question pure language-model reasoning under real perceptual conditions.
arxiv-2503-12007:
Chen-Rong Liu and colleagues set the theoretical sensitivity limit for atom-based microwave sensors in a 2025 paper. Rydberg atoms, atoms puffed up to huge sizes, react strongly to microwaves and can measure electric fields with extreme delicacy. What the fundamental floor of that delicacy is, given photon shot noise and atomic response, had not been worked out in a full Fisher information framework.

Their framework derives Fisher information for slope detection and converts it into a sensitivity formula. With real cesium vapor parameters, the optimized sensitivity lands below a nanovolt per centimeter per root hertz, and stays there under moderate parameter changes. Experiments trail that floor mainly through technical noise, so the theory maps how much room remains to improve.
arxiv-2503-12307:
Jiahao Wu and seven co-authors present Swift4D, a method that rebuilds moving 3D scenes from new viewpoints. Their paper from twenty twenty-five uses 3D Gaussian Splatting, a fast scene format. Past methods slow down on motion and eat storage. Most of a scene is still, the team notes, yet old tools pay the motion cost for all of it.

Swift4D splits the scene's blobs into still and moving sets. A learned tag sorts each blob. Only moving blobs get time-based warps, via a compact 4D hash map. The two sets then merge for the final view. This split speeds training and cuts storage waste. On real data the method matched top quality while training far faster. It needed only a small store, and code is public.
arxiv-2503-13907:
Chao Dong, Yiyang Liao, Ziye Jia, Qihui Wu, and Lei Zhang design a collaborative surveillance system for drone networks, in a paper from twenty twenty-five. Drones now serve many fields, which strains airspace safety. Single-communication surveillance limits where drones can operate. Their model combines automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast with beyond-5G links.

Drones deploy hierarchically: a low-altitude central drone carries the 5G module, a high-altitude one carries the broadcast unit. The broadcast unit automatically shares flight information with nearby aircraft and ground stations. The authors derive channel performance for air-to-ground and air-to-air links. An on-board mobile edge computing algorithm then filters redundancy and repairs information loss. Simulations and experiments verified the design. The algorithm filtered out over half the transmitted data as redundant. Better trajectory observability should improve airspace safety and traffic management.
arxiv-2503-16707:
Jinlong Li, Cristiano Saltori, Fabio Poiesi, and Nicu Sebe present CUA-O3D, a model for open-vocabulary understanding of three-dimensional scenes, in a two thousand twenty-five computer vision paper. Open-vocabulary means the model can label objects described in free text, not just fixed categories.

Instead of relying on one vision-language model, CUA-O3D distills knowledge from CLIP, DINOv2, and Stable Diffusion together. A deterministic uncertainty estimate weighs each model's features, balancing semantic priors against geometric knowledge. Experiments on ScanNetV2 and Matterport3D show gains in open-vocabulary segmentation plus strong cross-domain alignment and spatial perception.
arxiv-2503-20207:
Peiyuan Ni and co-authors wrote this robotics paper, published in two thousand twenty-five, on teaching warehouse robots to pick metal parts out of bins. Cheap depth cameras struggle with shiny metal: depth data comes back patchy, and poses are often wrong.

Their system works in two stages. First, a reasoning step tests pose guesses against depth, collision, and edge rules to clean the raw data. A symmetry-aware filter then trims the pose list further, since many parts look the same when flipped. Second, the camera learns a scoring metric from the cleaned data, so it can train itself on new parts with no hand labels. Tests on a public data set and a new one from the team beat prior methods. The aim is bin-picking that needs far less human setup.
arxiv-2503-22407:
Dobrev keeps up a long step-by-step project on invariant differential operators for an exceptional Lie algebra. His work came out in 2025. The symmetry is the split real form of the exceptional Lie algebra F4. Invariant operators act between representation spaces and do not break that symmetry when they act. The build proceeds by induction from a maximal parabolic subalgebra. Reducible Verma modules mark the spots where such operators can live.

Dobrev works out which of those modules fit the chosen induction, and each module that fits yields an operator of its own. That classification is the main result of the work, set out as a full list. Past parts of the same project dealt with other algebras in the same way. Representation theory gains one more chapter done in full. Physics that rests on symmetry uses these operators in its models.
arxiv-2504-01307:
Wei Shi, Bin Wang, and Kai Liu build an invariants preserving integrator in two thousand twenty five. Many conservative equations hold several invariant functionals at once. KdV, Schrödinger, and Klein-Gordon systems are classic examples of the type. Schemes that keep all invariants are hard to design.

A discrete variational derivative anchors their construction from the start. Projection turns standard integrators into multiple invariant keepers. Accuracy order matches the underlying scheme, they prove. Concrete mass, momentum, and energy preserving KdV schemes follow. The semi analytical route keeps the method broadly usable.
arxiv-2504-02307:
Maria Rosaria Marulli, Jacopo Bonari, Pasqualantonio Pingue, and Marco Paggi wrote this paper in two thousand twenty-five. It tackles sticky contact between rough surfaces, where pull between the faces shapes how they press and cling.

The team feeds real surface data from an atomic force microscope straight into finite element models. Both the bumps of the surface and how the stickiness shifts from spot to spot come from the scans. A tweaked Lennard-Jones law, set spot by spot from the measured pull and lost energy, drives the contact. Tests on a mixed plastic sample, in flat and full three-dimensional form, show that shifts in stickiness and in the bulk matter as much as the bumps do.
arxiv-2504-04307:
Benjamin Castle and Assaf Hasson ask when an abelian variety can be reconstructed from bare group data plus one distinguished subvariety. Zilber had shown, using model theory, that a high-genus curve is determined by its Jacobian seen only as an abstract group with the curve's image marked. The authors generalize the question to arbitrary abelian and semi-abelian varieties.

Their main theorem characterizes exactly when the abstract data determine the pair in the strongest reasonable sense. Understanding this required a new theory of factorizations for such pairs, with unique factorization theorems proved in the final sections. In that language, determination holds precisely for simple pairs with the subvariety strictly between zero and full dimension.
arxiv-2504-05307:
Sowmya Sundaram, Rafael Gonçalves, and Mark Musen chase total recall in science data search by fixing metadata with AI. Their paper is from two thousand twenty-five; the pack row gives no title or year, so the text head is the source. Metadata records are often patchy or malformed, which hides data sets from search.

They pair GPT-4 with strict templates from the CEDAR store, which name each field and its allowed values. The model then cleans records in bulk to fit the template. On two big biology stores, recall of apt data sets leaps from under a fifth to near two thirds. The template path beats a plain data-dictionary path, and rival models trail the GPT-4 pairing.
arxiv-2504-05507:
Dale Worley reworks the axioms for gluing lattices, with modular, locally finite lattices in view. The paper from twenty twenty-five studies how blocks join into a sum lattice. Such lattices may rise without bound, though each cover step stays finite. Worley offers two axiom sets with opposed aims. One set is maximal, squeezing out all that can be read at once about a valid gluing.

The other set is minimal, asking the least that must be shown to prove a block system glues well. That lean set appears new in the literature. Its checks are strikingly local, touching only small intervals between two elements and their meet and join. Yet the glued whole keeps global modular traits, such as the diamond isomorphism. The contrast shows how local rules can force global order.
arxiv-2504-08607:
Abhinandan Bhattacharjee and co-authors brought in a reading method in 2025 for very faint ultrafast pulses of single photons. Such pulses can carry information in quantum methods, and builders want to shape their time and rate traits exactly. Checking them fully, though, has needed heavy equipment and complex rebuild software.

Their method, called FIREFLY, interferes varied rate parts of a pulse with each other using a device called a quantum pulse gate driven by a reference pulse. From those readings it reads out the pulse's spectral strength, phase, and coherence, with no heavy method needed. The team showed it on partially coherent pulses made by a down-conversion source, and added a spectral shear step that removes the need to know the reference pulse in advance.
arxiv-2504-11507:
Alessia Ferrara, Júlio Amando de Barros, Sophie Marie Koch, and Falk Wittel simulate wood densification in two thousand twenty five. Densified spruce gains stiffness and strength for products. Finite element runs track how the tissue folds under load. Protocols span steady compression and oscillatory excitation modes.

Shrinking hydrogel fillings drive a self densification variant too. Tracheid wall behavior is modeled as anisotropic in the runs. Moisture and delignification effects enter through a hierarchical scheme. Folding patterns differ by tissue type and protocol. Targeted profiles could tailor density for specific uses.
arxiv-2504-12107:
Raju Baral and six co-authors show two neutron scattering techniques on the HB-2A powder diffractometer in a two thousand twenty-five instruments paper. The setup sits at the High Flux Isotope Reactor.

Magnetic pair distribution function analysis reveals local spin ordering and suits materials with only short-range magnetic order. Half-polarized neutron powder diffraction measures the local susceptibility tensor, which pins down magnetic anisotropy. Used as one, the techniques expose local magnetic conduct that average structure hides. Example measures focus on frustrated magnets and reach cold levels below one hundred millikelvin, far colder than such tests usually achieve.
arxiv-2504-12307:
Gauthami and Chacko build a new chance spread by use of the Power Generalized DUS shift on the inverse Weibull spread. The shift counts in work on trust of gear, most for twin paths side by side. The inverse Weibull model is much used for life span data. The team works out the base chance traits of the new model.

Traits not known are gauged by best chance and by best yield of gaps. A mock run checks the gauges, and the trust trait that weighs two life spans is looked at. A fit to a real world data set shows the new model beats rival spreads. The team sets it out as a choice with give for work on trust and life span.
arxiv-2504-13307:
Tomasz Downarowicz, Benjamin Weiss, Mateusz Więcek, and Guohua Zhang prove a universality result for group subshifts in two thousand twenty-five. The group is infinite, countable, and amenable. The subshift has a trait called specification and holds a free element. Universal means it can mirror any free ergodic action of lower entropy.

They show such a subshift has positive topological entropy. For any free ergodic action below that bound, a shift invariant measure makes the two systems isomorphic. A key case is the K-shift, built from maximal spaced sets. If it holds a free element, it too is universal. The theorem is broad in scope.
arxiv-2504-16407:
Alper Cakan, Vipul Goyal, and Omri Shmueli construct a new quantum object, public-key quantum fire, in a twenty twenty-five paper. Quantum fire is a spread of quantum states that can be copied freely, yet cannot be turned into a classic string of bits. Past work could build it only with odd oracles or unproven guesses.

The trio builds it from a classical oracle and proves its safety outright. They then define a stronger form, quantum key-fire, where the copyable states act as keys, and prove a strong interactive safety for it. As a side result, they split two quantum rules that were thought to be one: no-cloning and no-teleportation.
arxiv-2504-17207:
Phillip Lee and five co-authors teach vision-language models to take other viewpoints in twenty twenty-five. Taking another's perspective is a key part of human visual understanding. It matters when people work with autonomous agents in shared spaces. Modern vision-language models, the authors note, are weak at this and lean hard toward their own viewpoint.

Humans shift perspective through mental imagery, using abstract inner pictures of a scene. The authors build a framework, Abstract Perspective Change, on that idea. The model forms an abstract image of the scene and then simulates how it would look from elsewhere. Readers get a method aimed at closing a clear gap between model and human perception.
arxiv-2505-01407:
Ranjeet Kumar, Newton Nath, Rahul Srivastava, and Sushant Yadav build a particle physics model that ties two puzzles together. Their paper, from two thousand twenty-five, links dark matter and the tiny masses of neutrinos. It uses a flavor symmetry called A4, whose breaking leaves behind a dark symmetry. That leftover symmetry keeps the dark matter particle stable.

In the model, neutrino masses arise through a loop-based inverse seesaw path. The scheme explains the two measured gaps between neutrino masses seen in oscillation tests. It allows both normal and inverted mass orderings. It also makes sharp links between the sum of neutrino masses and other test values. Limits on scalar masses narrow where the dark matter mass can sit.
arxiv-2505-04707:
Serena Cronin, Alberto Bolatto, and colleagues map the hot wind blowing out of a nearby starburst galaxy in a 2025 astronomy study. The galaxy NGC 253 drives a superwind of ionized gas, visible in hydrogen light. An integral field spectrograph on a large telescope records a spectrum at every point of the image. This lets the team separate gas in the disk from gas in the two walls of the outflow cone.

Fitting several velocity components to the bright emission lines in each pixel yields the wind's physical conditions. Knowing temperature, density, and speed in the warm phase shows how much energy and metal the wind carries away.
arxiv-2505-07407:
Asif Manzoor Hasan, Pedro Costa, Johan Larsson, and Rene Pecnik build scale rules for two marks of fast, squeezed flow near a wall. Their paper is from two thousand twenty-five.

The marks are the size of wall pressure swings and the peak of flow speed swings along the stream. Both shift when the fluid's traits vary and when its bulk gives under pressure. The team writes each mark as a series in powers of a set Mach count. The lead term uses the known rules for calm flows, with an adjusted count for drag. Next terms, set by fits to set cases, catch the squeeze effects. The rules hold across many test flows.
arxiv-2505-07707:
Matthew Jankousky, Dimitar Pashov, Ross Larsen, and three co-authors ask how electrons can move free in this two thousand twenty-five paper. Atom mess tends to trap them in place, yet some amorphous solids show band-like flow though they have no crystal form. The team built a first-principles account of electron form and flow for such solids. It pairs a new statement of the amorphous state with a many-body method.

They used amorphous indium oxide as the test case. The way matched the band-like cast of the flow electrons and their mobility, which is capped by the mess. The sums showed why they stay free to move, and why band spread lasts with no long-range order. The work gives a tool to forecast traits. It fits a class of solids that count in electronics, where mess can not be dodged yet flow stays neat.
arxiv-2505-10207:
Allen Ibiapina, Minh Hang Nguyen, Mikaël Rabie, and Cléophée Robin define graph coloring for temporal graphs, in a paper from twenty twenty-five. Classical coloring forbids adjacent vertices sharing a color. In dynamic graphs, that notion is ambiguous across time steps. Their coloring must stay proper at every step, including during transitions between snapshots.

Compatibility between consecutive snapshots ensures properness survives each transition. The minimum colors needed is the graph's temporal chromatic number.
