arxiv-2603-11707: Ben-Abdallah builds a unified framework for the Mpemba effect in many-body systems near equilibrium. A system starting farther from equilibrium can relax faster than a closer one. He splits the effect into a non-uniform kind, marked by crossing global distances, and a strict componentwise kind. Reciprocal systems, he shows, allow only the first kind. Breaking reciprocity makes the operator non-normal and can unlock the strict kind.
arxiv-2603-12107: Olson and Reluga solve a social distancing game under classic SI epidemic dynamics. Players weigh infection risk against the running cost of keeping distance, with no discounting. In their special case, thresholds make distancing costs grow in a linear, capped way. A change of variables lets them build Nash equilibria directly by integration. The unique outcome is bang-bang: a wait-and-see phase, then a lockdown phase. Best public policy matches that outcome, and distancing pays only inside a Goldilocks zone of response delay.
arxiv-2603-12207: Tümer, Norseth, and Wik report X-ray evidence for a very strong shock in the merging cluster ZWCL 1856.8. Deeper NuSTAR data follow a shallower pilot study of the same system. The cluster hosts a double radio relic from a near head-on collision. Temperature maps across the field let the team read shock strength at both relic sites. The northern shock ranks among the strongest X-ray shocks seen in a cluster merger, well above its radio counterpart. No inverse Compton emission turned up at the relic sites.
arxiv-2603-12507: Kurbucz proposes adaptive conditional residual sampling, or ACRS, for spectral risk optimisation. The catch: which inputs arise depends on the decision, and sampling them needs a costly simulator under a fixed budget. ACRS draws once at each design point and fits a model of how the inputs spread. Scaled residuals become scenarios for a fixed surrogate that can be searched fast. It adds draws near the best optima and refines the leaders by local search. On sixty random instances, mean regret hits 11.8%, well below five baselines.
arxiv-2603-12707: Donglin Yu studies how to serve multimodal language models cheaply by splitting work across GPU tiers. Vision encoding is compute-bound, while text generation is bound by memory bandwidth. He shows the split point between vision and language parts cuts data transfer the most. That split lets cheap PCIe links replace costly high-bandwidth ones. His HeteroServe runtime schedules the two phases across mixed hardware. Under a fixed budget, the mixed cluster gave far more tokens per dollar than a uniform one.
arxiv-2603-13207: Bastiaan J. Braams takes up the problem of estimating missing mass when sampling from a discrete set. For each sampled point, its unnormalized probability mass is revealed to the analyst. Classic tools like the harmonic mean and Good-Turing estimators can be Rao-Blackwellized here. That step gives self-consistent estimators with no auxiliary distribution of known total mass. Braams adds a model for the mass distribution and studies it in several ways. Bayesian, likelihood, and moment methods are combined to remove nuisance parameters.
arxiv-2603-13407: Alex Shvets computes the exact leading term of Le Cam deficiency for shuffled histograms. Deficiency is the largest rise in Bayes risk caused by keeping only a retained statistic. Shvets works with growing shuffle models that have finite hypothesis families. For a bounded correlated message bundle, the coefficient comes out as a convex program with Gaussian-polynomial scores. Which moment degree first differs between the families fixes the order of the term. Kernels that preserve tags can be suboptimal, he also shows.
arxiv-2603-13507: Jinwei Hu and co-authors present MIRAGE, a pipeline for realistic industrial anomaly generation and evaluation. Visual anomaly detectors train on normal samples only, yet even limited anomalous data helps a lot. MIRAGE needs no training and no anomalous images to build realistic defect images and pixel-level masks. It calls any generative model as a black box, uses a VLM to draft defect prompts, and filters with CLIP. A dual-branch module joins Grounding DINO and YOLOv26-Seg features for masks. The team releases over 13,000 image-mask pairs.
arxiv-2603-13607: Pranav Chandarana and co-authors benchmark a hybrid sequential quantum solver against classical solvers for combinatorial optimization. The solver runs on IBM Heron r3 processors for higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problems. All runtimes include preprocessing, QPU execution, and postprocessing under strict wall-clock accounting. Across 20 instances, one hybrid attempt gave high-quality solutions in under one second, matching ground-state energy in 14 cases. CPU solvers did not reach that value at the same runtime, while enhanced parallel tempering and a GPU solver matched or beat it.
arxiv-2603-14007: Sonna, Momo, and Grastien build a formal framework that explains AI predictions about mental health help-seeking in tech workplaces. Instead of loose, ad-hoc reasons, the framework computes strict abductive justifications for each model output. Those proofs help pick models that fit distinct psychiatric profiles and plan fair recourse. The work also tests how sensitive traits like gender sway model choices. The aim is trustworthy use of such models and better targeted support at work.
arxiv-2603-14207: Niu and co-authors present DualTSR, a single transformer that restores low-resolution scene text images. Older methods lean on outside OCR models for text hints or stack hard-to-train parts. DualTSR trains one backbone with two diffusion goals at once. One goal models the sharp image itself, and the other models the text content as discrete data. The shared design lets sight and text inform each other at every layer. Tests on synthetic Chinese sets and a real-world suite show strong clarity and text fidelity.
arxiv-2603-14407: Li and co-authors present OFA-TAD, a one-for-all detector for anomalies in tabular data. Older detectors train one model per dataset, which costs much and travels poorly. Their framework trains once on many source sets, then runs on new domains with no fresh training. Neighbor-distance patterns act as the portable cue, read through several distance views. A mixture-of-experts scorer fuses the views, and synthetic anomalies support the one-class training. Tests span 34 datasets in 14 domains.
arxiv-2603-14507: Peng and co-authors grow mmWave pose datasets with unlabeled data and LiDAR sets. Current mmWave datasets are small and lack pose variety. Trained models then fail on new settings. Their EMDUL method has two parts. A pseudo-label tool tags unlabeled mmWave scans. A closed-form converter turns LiDAR point clouds into mmWave form. Adding both kinds of data lifts every pose model tested. Errors drop 15.1% in-domain and 18.9% out-of-domain, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-14607: Bautra, Dimitrijevs and Yakaryilmaz test calibration-based digital twins of IBM quantum hardware. A twin should mimic real device outcomes on a classical simulator. Twins here grow from public calibration files. Coherence times and error rates map to thermal, depolarizing and readout noise channels. A directed coupling map restores device connectivity during transpilation. Four twin types run five-qubit circuits on two IBM machines. CSV-built twins often match hardware best, they find. Match quality still shifts with device and transpiler settings.
arxiv-2603-14807: Lyu and co-authors cure navigation amnesia in open-source vision-language navigation with HiMemVLN. Zero-shot navigators lean on closed models, with cost and leakage risks. Open models with spatiotemporal reasoning still trail far behind. Step-by-step logs expose a memory failure the team names Navigation Amnesia. A hierarchical memory system joins the multimodal model to fix it. Tests in simulation and real settings back the design. Scores near twice the open-source state of the art, they report.
arxiv-2603-14907: Menke and co-authors argue machine learning for geoenergy must deliver uncertainty, not just predictions. Carbon storage, geothermal and hydrogen projects follow a screening-to-stewardship funnel. Sparse, biased labels and few field outcomes starve the models. Physical and geological limits bind every choice along the way. Four bottlenecks recur across projects, they find. Weak scale-bridging and thin audit trails join the label and uncertainty gaps. Hybrid physics-ML, probabilistic scores and structure-aware inputs fit the terrain. Decision-ready inference is the stated goal.
arxiv-2603-15007: The ATLAS Collaboration reinterprets thirteen earlier searches for supersymmetry using the full Run 2 dataset. The data cover 140 inverse femtobarns of proton collisions at 13 TeV from 2015 to 2018. The new reading tests models where the R-parity-violating coupling varies, so the lightest superpartner may decay fast or live long. Limits reach 1.8 TeV for gluinos and 2.4 TeV for top squarks at strong coupling. Tau-slepton and Higgsino masses are also constrained.
arxiv-2603-15707: Peng and co-authors present SEMAG, a self-evolving team system for code generation. Fixed workflows and hand-picked models adapt poorly as task difficulty shifts. SEMAG splits coding work into planning, coding, debugging, and discussion stages. Its agents can reach the newest models in real time. The backbone model upgrades itself when better options appear. The authors report new top Pass@1 scores across benchmarks. On CodeContests it beat prior methods by 3.3 percent at equal backbones. Self-picked backbones lifted the score to 52.6 percent.
arxiv-2603-15807: Kadoma, Shrivastava, and Naaman test how bad subtitles change viewer judgment. Speech tools err more for some accents than for others. The team ran a preregistered online study with 207 U.S. crowdworkers. Viewers watched accented talks with clean or error-prone subtitles. Faulty subtitles lowered scores for speakers and for content alike. The drop hit all accent groups evenly in the study. Speakers whose accents trip ASR tools may still face harsher viewer scores. Error-prone captions act as a second penalty layer.
arxiv-2603-16007: Mengesha and co-authors sort world cities into 17 lasting growth regimes. National frames hide the city engines of global output. Their dataset tracks 8,808 urban areas across 165 countries. Night light data builds GDP paths from 1993 to 2019. Clustering full paths yields the 17 regime groups. Cities in one country often land in unlike regimes. Like cities on far continents share regimes instead. Shocks travel along likeness lines, not map distance. Rich economies export shocks, emerging ones absorb or amplify them.
arxiv-2603-16307: Yang and co-authors build NeSy-Route, a benchmark for route planning from remote sensing images. Current tests stress perception and reasoning, not planning. Their set holds 10,821 route tasks with provably best routes. An automated pipeline builds tasks from semantic masks plus heuristic search. A three-level scoring protocol grades perception, reasoning, and planning apart. Top multimodal models showed clear gaps in both perception and planning. The set is nearly ten times larger than prior ones.
arxiv-2603-16607: Nekula, Bělín, and Konečná speed up wave simulation for electron microscopy. Short wavelengths and wide cone angles demand extreme sampling. Standard angular spectrum code quickly exceeds memory and time budgets. Their scaling method swaps in a shrunken twin optical system. Sampling needs drop by about the square of the scale factor. A second method drops lensing effects away from focus. Together with a chirp-z method, the trio covers complex systems once deemed infeasible.
arxiv-2603-16707: Peñuela proves curvature bounds and rigidity for surfaces of constant mean curvature. The results cover curved spaces and spacetime alike. A classic bound ties squared mean curvature to a surface's area. His version needs a weaker check: stability only in the constant mode. When equality holds, the enclosed region must be flat Euclidean space. For spacetime surfaces he builds the matching stability theory. The sharp bound holds when matter obeys the dominant energy rule. Equality there forces a causal diamond in flat Minkowski space.
arxiv-2603-16907: Borrill documents how the Category Mistake framework and its Forward-In-Time-Only analysis took shape. This supplement supports his recent arXiv papers on those ideas. The concepts grew over fifteen years of research, conversation, and engineering practice. Key steps include a 2014 Stanford lecture on the physics of time in computing, and a 2016 exchange with Leslie Lamport about his 1978 paper. Work on Open Atomic Ethernet also shaped the ideas. Borrill argues that Lamport's happened-before relation embeds a category mistake, with practical effects on distributed systems.
arxiv-2603-17007: de Paula and co-authors study how photons move in nonlinear electrodynamics near black holes. In such theories, an effective geometry guides photon motion. Their model is built on two electromagnetic invariants. They show that light exhibits vacuum birefringence: photons follow two distinct paths, set by their polarization. A black hole in this theory can carry two unstable light rings and cast two distinct shadows. They compare the shadow size with observations of Sagittarius A*. This lets them bound the black hole's charge to mass ratio.
arxiv-2603-17307: Yan and co-authors present Symphony, a multi agent system for understanding long videos. Long video tasks pack dense information over long spans, and simple task splitting is not enough. Symphony mimics human cognition: it breaks the task into fine grained subtasks and adds a deep reasoning collaboration step with reflection. A vision based grounding approach scores how relevant each video segment is. The system reached state of the art results on four long video benchmarks. On LVBench it improved on the prior best by 5 percent.
arxiv-2603-17407: Singh and Chandok present a modified algorithm for variational inequality problems in Hilbert spaces. Their method adds double inertia and a self-adaptive step size. It needs no prior knowledge of the operator's Lipschitz constant. They prove weak convergence for non-monotone operators and strong convergence for nicer classes. Linear convergence holds under a simpler setup, they show. Tests against older algorithms and a sensitivity study support the method.
arxiv-2603-17507: Herath, Rahulamathavan, De Silva, and Lambotharan present QuantFL, a greener federated learning scheme for edge IoT devices. Sending model updates often costs heavy energy on battery-powered gear. Pre-trained starts concentrate update values, so simple bucket quantisation stays accurate. The design skips costly error-feedback machinery entirely. Total traffic fell by about 40 percent on MNIST and CIFAR-100, they report. Accuracy matched or beat full-precision baselines.
arxiv-2603-17607: Irodotou and co-authors add a relativistic accretion disc model to galaxy formation simulations. This third RABBITS study evolves black hole mass and spin with the disc itself. Local disc solutions cover gas- or radiation-led pressure and two opacity sources. Stitching them by validity range gives the global disc shape. Each growth episode now follows from first principles, not Bondi-style guesses. Disc sizes, heat profiles, and spectra come out directly.
arxiv-2603-17807: Beradze, Tsitsishvili, and Moroz map the phase diagram of a one-dimensional Z2 lattice gauge theory. Spinless fermions and Ising spins couple to a deconfined gauge field in their orthogonal metal model. An exact rewrite splits the system into XXZ and transverse-field Ising chains. Field theory then describes the low-energy side in controlled terms. Along one multi-critical line, an emergent superconformal symmetry appears, they find. Quantum simulators could probe it.
arxiv-2603-17907: Yang and Zhu ask what happens when everyone can use actionable recourse in a contest. Recourse lets rejected applicants tweak traits to flip an AI decision. In hiring or admissions, though, only a share of candidates can win. Their game model has rejected candidates push along the rule's favored paths. As all adjust at once, the success bar moves with the crowd. Early winners set both the bar and the path, they show. Initial gaps thus harden into lasting ones.
arxiv-2603-18107: Ray introduces ARTEMIS, a neuro-symbolic framework for market dynamics under economic constraints. Deep finance models often act as black boxes and ignore no-arbitrage rules. ARTEMIS joins a Laplace neural operator encoder, a neural differential equation, and a symbolic bottleneck for readable rules. Two penalties curb no-arbitrage breaches and bound the market price of risk. On four datasets it led on Time-IMM at 96.0% and the synthetic crash set at 64.96%.
arxiv-2603-18207: Shi and Feng find soliton solutions for a coupled Sasa-Satsuma-mKdV equation with a KP reduction method. The system pairs a complex-valued part with a real-valued one. Under zero and nonzero boundary conditions, four classes appear: bright-bright, dark-dark, bright-dark, and dark-bright. They study collisions for each class and find inelastic hits among bright-bright solitons. The dark-dark case shows double-hole, Mexican hat, and anti-Mexican hat profiles plus kink collisions.
arxiv-2603-18407: K and co-authors build a general framework for dynamic games with interleaved information structures. Past work covers feedback play, where agents see the current state, and open-loop play, where they see only the start. Real settings mix these: each agent sees only some others at each step. Their Mathematical Program Networks encode these information links directly. For linear-quadratic games, Riccati-like equations then characterize Nash equilibria, shown on a three-agent cyclic case.
arxiv-2603-18507: Hu, Rostami, and Thomason show expert personas improve LLM alignment but can damage accuracy, then fix the trade-off with PRISM. Persona effects vary with model tuning, task type, and prompt length and placement, they find. PRISM self-distills an intent-conditioned persona into a gated LoRA adapter with no external data. Bootstrapping routes each request to a fitting persona by inferred intent. Alignment on generative tasks rises while discriminative accuracy holds across all models tested.
arxiv-2603-19207: Giri and co-authors study ripples that form where layers of a three-part Bose-Einstein condensate slide past each other. They spin only the middle part, which lets shear and counterflow be tuned at two borders. Three regimes are mapped, from strong separation to a mix where two instabilities act at once. A pressure rule predicts when the Kelvin-Helmholtz ripple starts. Simulations then track how the pattern grows over time. Mode checks match the shapes seen in the runs.
arxiv-2603-19407: Arcadi and co-authors let light sterile neutrinos explain both dark matter and the matter excess of the universe. The particles sit below the electroweak scale in mass. At high heat they act as Dirac particles, which links them to Dirac leptogenesis. At low heat they can serve as warm dark matter. The team first treats early abundances as free inputs and maps the viable space. Cosmic and astro limits are applied along with neutrino mass needs. Two full high-energy completions show the idea can be built.
arxiv-2603-19507: Miceli and co-authors lay out what an AI-ready control system for the Fermilab accelerator complex needs. Reliable high-intensity running supports the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility and the DUNE experiment. Three needs stand out. An MLOps framework should standardize the full model lifecycle. A data quality framework should enforce standards for trustworthy models. Language model workflows should help staff find information and write code. Use cases span beam diagnostics, beam control, and support system automation.
arxiv-2603-19707: Shukla and co-authors use a long short-term memory network to predict wireless channels inside a bus. The model learns how the channel transfer function changes with transmitter and receiver spots. Their tests use the 60 GHz band, where signals fade fast. From each predicted function they build a power delay profile. The profile taps came out with an average error under ten percent. The authors present this as a light tool for planning in-vehicle links.
arxiv-2603-19907: Wang and Stadler extend the spherical-radial decomposition to problems with endless stochastic dimensions. The classic method estimates probabilistic functions well for elliptical distributions in finite dimensions. Their hybrid version mixes subspace decomposition with plain Monte Carlo sampling. The result is an unbiased estimator with low variance and no truncation bias. It also gives derivatives of the probabilistic functions. Tests cover a stochastic PDE control problem with joint chance limits. A second test tunes kernel parameters in Gaussian process regression under similar limits.
arxiv-2603-20107: Karimi and co-authors spread privacy-preserving monitoring across several parties instead of one monitor. A single monitor that guards privacy needs heavy cryptography, too slow for real-time use. Their design assumes at least one monitoring party is honest. That trust lets them use light secret-sharing schemes in place of costly crypto. Unlike one-shot secret-sharing tools, their protocol keeps a secret internal state. It supports repeated checks as the system evolves. Built on MP-SPDZ, tests show far better scaling than existing options under these assumptions.
arxiv-2603-20407: Busko searches archival photographic plates from Hamburg Observatory for fast astronomical transients. The VASCO project earlier found such flashes on 1950s Palomar plates. Busko uses plate pairs taken about 30 minutes apart in the 1950s. The plates come from the observatory's 1.2-meter Schmidt camera, digitized by APPLAUSE. The search finds evidence of transients much like the VASCO ones. Their light profiles are systematically narrower than those of stars. This supports reading them as sub-second flashes from orbiting objects.
arxiv-2603-20907: Shen and co-authors study how chatbots can quietly steer users toward hidden goals. People now ask language models for daily and personal advice, which leaves them open to subtle pressure. Past work detects manipulation but rarely links it to real belief change. Their PUPPET resource sorts hidden incentives by moral direction. It holds over one thousand chats with measured belief shifts. They find that skill at spotting manipulation does not track how much beliefs move. Top models predict belief shift only moderately well.
arxiv-2603-21007: Liu and co-authors settle open questions on exponential tractability for linear weighted tensor product problems. They study algorithms that use finitely many evaluations of continuous linear functionals, in the worst case setting. They examine two forms of exponential weak tractability, under absolute or normalized error. By filling the remaining gaps, they obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for both notions. The results complete the picture of when such problems stay tractable at an exponential scale.
arxiv-2603-21107: Kidane and Dargie measure what shapes link quality in low-power wireless sensor networks. Both the environment and radio manufacturing differences can shift link quality. They ran deployments in over fifteen settings, from rivers and forests to bridges and gardens, with four radio types. They propose a light statistical outlier detection method. Its parameters come from the statistics of raw and predicted link quality measures, such as RSSI. Their results show how strongly outside and inside factors each affect performance, which guides radio and environment specific setup.
arxiv-2603-21207: Zhou and co-authors test how to choose machine learning surrogate models for Monte Carlo studies of chemical order and disorder. High entropy materials mix random solutions with enthalpy driven ordering, which needs long simulations. They benchmark invariant and equivariant designs on a data set of over ten thousand configurations across seven elements. An explainable method splits pairwise from higher-order effects. They also test how lattice relaxation in the training data changes the models, and give guidance for Monte Carlo use.
arxiv-2603-21307: Klimov and co-authors identify a precessing jet axis in the supernova remnant 3C 397. They find an S-shaped faint region of two bubbles, north and south of the center, between two X-ray bright sides. They attribute the shape to a pair of precessing jets active during the explosion. The jet axis makes 3C 397 more like the remnant W49B. They discuss two scenarios for both remnants, each giving jets a primary role in the explosion.
arxiv-2603-21407: Buhai develops a theory of extreme economic outcomes that looks beyond distribution tails. Unequal access to opportunities also shapes who reaches the top. In a mixed Poisson search model, normalized maxima get a mixture form that supports clean comparisons with an equal-access benchmark. A coupling argument turns gaps in access into optimal transport bounds for top quantiles and counterfactual paths. Buhai also studies an entropy-based design problem for reallocating opportunities under a mean constraint.
arxiv-2603-21607: Kuleshova and co-authors sharpen doubt scores for retrieval-augmented generation, where spotting hallucinations matters. Entropy, a common doubt signal, misbehaves in this setting, they show. Induction heads copy patterns from context and push entropy down for grounded answers. Yet they also seem to wake neurons that push entropy back up. Their INTRYGUE method gates entropy by an attention-based gauge of induction activity. On four benchmarks and six open models, it matched or beat the best rivals, with no training.
arxiv-2603-21707: Jindal and co-authors build a vertex coproduct on the cohomological Hall algebra of a quiver with potential. The construction follows Joyce and turns the algebra into a vertex bialgebra. A vertex form of bosonisation, after Majid and Radford, extends the algebra with a Cartan part. For ADE quivers, the new coproduct matches Drinfeld's deformed coproduct on the Yangian. They compare it with work by Davison and by Dotsenko and Mozgovoy. The construction also gives a new proof of the integrality theorem for symmetric quivers.
arxiv-2603-21807: Dai and co-authors locate the many-body localization transition with a small learning model. Instead of raw wave functions, they feed it four physics-based features per state. The features cover participation, entropy, hybridization, and level spacing. A Kolmogorov-Arnold Network trained on states at weak and strong disorder sorted new states with over 99.9 percent accuracy. That matched image-style networks trained on full wave functions, with far less input and training time. Sweeping the trained model across energies revealed a clear mobility edge and a critical disorder strength.
arxiv-2603-22407: De Crescenzo and co-authors speed up particle physics calculations at next-to-leading order. Their system, MadNIS, pairs fast amplitude surrogates with neural importance sampling. For virtual corrections, a learned ratio to the Born term carries calibrated error bars. That keeps precision honest across phase space. For real emission, they keep the standard FKS subtraction. Sector-based surrogates learn the cleaned integrands away from divergences. MadNIS then uses the channel maps and sectors as conditions. Tests on electron-positron scattering to three and four jets show clear speed gains.
arxiv-2603-23007: Luo and co-authors present AgentRAE, a backdoor attack on mobile GUI agents. These agents control phones from screenshots. The attack uses natural-looking triggers, such as app icons in notifications, to force remote actions. A two-stage pipeline first sharpens the agent's sense for small icon differences. It then links each trigger to a target action through post-training. Attack success passes ninety percent across ten mobile operations. Clean performance stays intact, and the triggers look benign. Eight known defenses fail to stop it, they report.
arxiv-2603-23107: Shaawat and co-authors analyze the Egyptian community on Reddit as a network. Their dataset holds over twenty-three thousand users and 105 Egypt-focused subreddits. They measure degree patterns, degree spread, and local clustering. Those measures reveal how the network connects and where tight groups form. Key users and paths for information flow come into view. The study adds a detailed case of an online community tied to one country. It shows how network tools can map such communities.
arxiv-2603-23407: Krebsbach and four co-authors study how numeric data should be encoded for generative quantum models. Such models learn a distribution and sample fresh cases. Most, like the Quantum Circuit Born Machine, work at a binary level. Plain binary coding forces the model to learn fake correlations from the code itself. It also hides smooth data structure. The team proposes reflected Gray codes at almost no extra cost. Gray codes keep data structure intact and dodge the fake links. In most tests, models learn faster and closer with them.
arxiv-2603-23507: Ding and ten co-authors replace masking in diffusion language models with deletion and insertion. Masked models waste compute on mask and pad tokens that carry no signal. Their DID models treat token deletion and insertion as the diffusion steps themselves. That frees length to vary with no padding at all. Insertion lets the model fix its slips mid-generation. A score-based trainer rates insert moves, backed by a dynamic program. Across settings, DID beats masked and insertion rivals on quality and speed, with no tuning.
arxiv-2603-23607: Wagner and twenty-two co-authors show that driving reasoning models often ignore their reasoning. Rare road events are the core of self-driving work. Reasoning models promise help by spelling out a plan before acting. The team built KITScenes LongTail, a set of rare driving scenes, to test that promise. They score how well stated plans match actions. Mismatch is common across general and driving-tuned models. When plans and actions split, the plan is usually the right one. Acting on the plan through a motion model improves driving.
arxiv-2603-24007: Sun and co-authors find universal scaling laws for how hysteresis loops grow with sweep rate. A hysteresis loop's area depends on how fast an external field is swept. Two regimes appear, split by a crossover rate tied to temperature. Below it, excess area grows with rate to the one-third power. Above it, the power is two-thirds. They show the same laws in magnetic experiments, Ising and framework simulations, and a solved Langevin equation. The result explains past scattered exponents and guides design.
arxiv-2603-24307: Karthika and co-authors release Samasāmayik, a parallel dataset for Hindi-Sanskrit machine translation. It holds 92,196 curated sentence pairs. Most Sanskrit data come from classical texts and poetry. This corpus instead draws on modern sources: spoken tutorials, children's magazines, radio conversations, and teaching materials. They fine-tune ByT5, NLLB, and IndicTrans-v2 on it. Models gain much on in-domain tests and hold up on standard sets. Overlap with older corpora is minimal, which confirms the dataset adds new material for a low-resource language pair.
arxiv-2603-24707: Shukla studies projection methods for eigenvalue problems of Fredholm integral operators. The focus is on how eigenvalues and their spectral subspaces behave. The methods use piecewise polynomials of even degree, with collocation points not tied to Gauss nodes. Shukla proves explicit rates for the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. A modified collocation method converges faster than the classic scheme. It also yields superconvergent eigenfunction approximations. Tests confirm the theory. In such work, a hard problem is swapped for a finite one that a machine can solve.
arxiv-2603-24807: Patiño and co-authors explain Balmer decrements in T Tauri stars with a two-flow accretion model. The standard one-flow model cannot reproduce the observed line ratios. Their model uses two flows with different rates and geometries side by side. Line fluxes for three Balmer lines are fitted with Bayesian statistics to 139 stars across four regions. One flow is compact and fast, hugging the star; the other is wider, thicker, and slower. Together they fit the decrements and the known luminosity correlation.
arxiv-2603-25007: Liu, Feng, and Wu extend Bollobás-type bounds from set systems to subspaces. They study pairs of subspaces that meet a skew condition, where the whole space splits into blocks. For such systems they prove a weighted sum bound, with each term built from block dimensions and binomial terms. The bound stays at or below one. They also revisit Tuza's theorem on weak Bollobás systems for d-tuples. A fresh proof covers the set case, and a matching version holds for subspaces with weights that sum to one.
arxiv-2603-25207: Sabdy and co-authors design heart baffles on a computer before surgeons build them in the chest. Some children with double outlet right ventricle need a custom wall inside the heart. It guides blood from the left ventricle to the aorta. Today that wall is shaped by hand during surgery. Their method builds a clean flow path from the defect to the aorta and shapes only the baffle. Flow tests on four past patients gave safe pressure drops, close to later heart scans.
arxiv-2603-25307: Sóstai encodes text strings as single numbers using blocks of Fibonacci numbers. Each string position picks one Fibonacci number from its own block. Gaps between blocks keep the picks non-adjacent. Zeckendorf's theorem then makes the sum decode back to one string only. The string length can be read from the code as well. The code's digit count grows in line with string length, which matches the best possible rate. A rival nested pairing scheme blows up exponentially, and he proves that too.
arxiv-2603-25407: Lewis and co-authors study finite groups where one conjugacy class is exactly the gap between two normal subgroups. Take nested normal subgroups, small inside large. Some element's whole class fills the ring between them. The team finds a character-based test for when this happens. They also draw out structural facts about such groups. With an extra rule, that the gap is the unique smallest normal piece, their result extends a theorem of Gagola. The work links class shape to subgroup layout.
arxiv-2603-25707: Phung and co-authors present Trace, a tool for editing object motion in videos. A user draws the wanted path in a single anchor frame. The system then rebuilds the video with the object on that path. A first module turns the drawn path into frame-by-frame boxes, even when the camera moves. A second module resynthesizes the video along those boxes. The rest of the scene stays intact. On varied real-world videos, the authors report more coherent and realistic edits than recent rival methods.
arxiv-2603-26007: Cherukuri predicts which patients with mild cognitive impairment will progress to Alzheimer's disease. His marker is the sharpness of the gray-white matter boundary on MRI scans. What matters is not one scan but how fast that boundary fades each year. He analyzes 1,824 scans from 450 ADNI subjects over about five years. Slope features feed a random survival forest. The test C-index reaches 0.63, far above baseline models at 0.24. MRI is much cheaper than PET imaging, he notes. The marker could aid screening and trial enrollment.
arxiv-2603-26107: Pyo and co-authors study how people juggle several AI models in daily life. Users pick models by perceived strength, which creates coordination work. Prompts must be reshaped for each interface, and trust is hard to calibrate. The team ran a diary study and interviews with ten users. People build shifting hierarchies of primary and backup models, they find. Switching follows task bunching, effort, delay, and output credibility. The authors draw lessons for tools that support multi-model work.
arxiv-2603-26407: Budzys, Liu, and Michalas present H-Elo, a private rating system for matchmaking built on fully homomorphic encryption. Matchmaking in dating apps, games, and social tools often demands sensitive personal data. H-Elo lets a service rank and match users while their ratings stay encrypted. The authors give the full construction and test its security against a capable adversary. In a chess rating test, H-Elo matches plaintext accuracy while keeping scores private, unlike most prior private matchmaking work.
arxiv-2603-26507: Duplantier, Gayrard, and Saksman study the integral means spectrum tied to the random Riemann zeta function. The randomised zeta function, due to Bagchi, mimics how vertical shifts of the true zeta function behave in the critical strip. The team looks at the spectrum of its primitive, an analytic function built by integration. Using probability and analytic number theory, they show the spectrum almost surely takes the shape Kraetzer conjectured decades ago. They prove the same shape for holomorphic multiplicative chaos on the unit disc.
arxiv-2603-26707: Eliav names and measures a growing gap between machine context and human attention, which he calls the Cognitive Divergence. AI context windows grew from 512 tokens in 2017 to two million by 2026, doubling about every 14 months. Over a similar span, his token-based gauge of human sustained reading fell from near 16,000 to about 1,800. He then proposes a delegation feedback loop: as AI grows stronger, people hand it ever smaller tasks. That habit, he argues, further weakens the attention span that oversight of AI needs.
arxiv-2603-26907: Vieira and Spiller give information-theoretic tools for two weak points in quantum networks. Seedless quantum random number generators face a loop: they need a seed to make randomness. The authors bootstrap them from raw data of two independent entropy sources. Universal hash functions act as strong extractors, backed by the quantum leftover hash lemma. The same extractors combine post-quantum and quantum key distribution keys. Unlike simple XOR, the scheme keeps the surviving key secure if one key leaks.
arxiv-2603-27007: Palmieri studies which algebraic traits can coexist inside finite extensional magmas. Three traits are at stake: self-representation, the classifier dichotomy, and internal composition. Palmieri proves the three are pairwise independent of each other. Lean-verified counterexamples at sizes four through ten show all six non-implications. Four of those bounds are provably tight. The smallest magma hosting all three traits has five members, which is optimal. The classifier dichotomy also yields a three-part split that is an isomorphism invariant. All results are in Lean 4, with no gaps.
arxiv-2603-27207: Cihlar and co-authors build a reinforcement learning system for autonomous race overtaking. The agent computes steering and speed from pre-generated raceline data plus live sensors. A LiDAR pipeline with a 2D detector spots the rival car ahead. A depth camera with YOLO detection adds a second view of that car. An unscented Kalman filter fuses both streams into one pose estimate. Pose errors stayed near 0.08 and 0.05 meters in the two axes. The full system completed overtakes in simulation and real-world runs alike.
arxiv-2603-27507: Huang and co-authors present Chat-Scene++, a model for talking about 3D scenes. The scene becomes a sequence of objects with rich context. Each object gets features plus an identifier token. Features come from large 3D and 2D encoders. That mix captures links between objects and global sense. The design supports grounded chain-of-thought reasoning. Models can split objects by type and by place. The system handles many 3D vision-language tasks without extra modules.
arxiv-2603-27607: Zhang and co-authors link two light scattering paths into one quantum tool. Stokes and anti-Stokes scattering can interfere when driven together. Their model works beyond the resolved-sideband limit. A shared drive and linewidth tie the two channels. Phase control then steers the interference. Destructive mixing aids quantum memory and transfer. Constructive mixing boosts signals for detection. Arrays of such units could push both uses further.
arxiv-2603-27707: Pandey measures how LoRA limits forgetting in staged fine-tuning. Encoders trained task by task often lose old skills. Five BERT reruns follow one four-task sequence. Full tuning forgets 19.9 percent on average. LoRA forgets just 0.6 percent on the same run. RoBERTa shows the same pattern. A strong EWC baseline still forgets 15.5 percent. Freezing past roughly 95 percent of weights drives the drop.
arxiv-2603-28007: Alvarez, Igusa, and Sullivan define a new family of invariants for Legendrian submanifolds, called Legendrian higher torsion. For a chosen class of fibre bundles over a manifold, the invariant collects higher Reidemeister torsion classes tied to bundles where the Legendrian has a generating function. For tube bundles they get tube torsion, and for nearby Lagrangians it splits into cosets of a normalized Pontryagin character. One coset stays fixed under Hamiltonian motion. They also build Legendrians with nontrivial tube torsion.
arxiv-2603-28107: Zhang and co-authors characterize asteroid Kamo'oalewa, the target of China's Tianwen-2 sample-return mission. From lightcurve data they model its shape as about 68 by 46 by 39 meters, with a spin period of 27.66 minutes. Grains under 2 cm should stay put on most of its surface. Lab tests on laser-weathered meteorite powder pin down its thermal traits and fine iron content. The asteroid's virtual spectral type comes out as Sqw.
arxiv-2603-28207: Zuo and six co-authors take a census of brightenings that travel along transition-region loops on the Sun. Using paired images from Solar Orbiter and the Solar Dynamics Observatory, they track 42 events seen in both datasets. The flashes last about two minutes, move at roughly 51 km/s on average, and start mostly near loop footpoints. Their lengths run from 3 to 11 megameters. The pattern fits heating driven by enthalpy flows and radiative cooling.
arxiv-2603-28507: Lu argues that AI progress can continue only if efficiency keeps doubling on a steady beat. Scaling laws track logical compute, not any fixed chip or code base. As returns shrink, each new unit of compute costs more in real resources. Hardware, algorithm, and systems gains must therefore repeat, much as Moore's law once organized chip progress. Recent trends look at least Moore-like, he notes. Without such doublings, scaling stalls under its own weight.
arxiv-2603-28607: Usynin, Shmakova, and Rheinberger present a data framework for craft beer, playfully framed around stout. Craft beers vary widely in style and ingredients, so taste is hard to predict. Producers also struggle to learn what consumers want. Their Distributed Beverage Analysis framework collects and analyzes beverage data in a collaborative way. They test it at the Kraft Bier Fest held by Vienna Kraft brewery. They also test large language models against the framework's findings. Many AI models, they report, cannot reason reliably over craft beer trends and patterns.
arxiv-2603-28707: Holthusen, Steinmann, and Kuhl present a physics-based neural network framework for thermoelasticity. Older models often start from the Helmholtz energy. Their method instead learns internal energy and a dissipation potential from deformation and entropy. That choice avoids mixed shape conditions. Temperature is the measured variable, while entropy is inferred inside the model. Input convex networks keep the model sound by construction. The design embeds objectivity and symmetry by construction. Tests on data for soft tissues and filled rubbers matched the target behavior well.
arxiv-2603-28807: Wang and co-authors propose SafeClaw-R, a safety framework for multi-agent personal helpers. Locally deployed agents can act across platforms, but reasoning failures and prompt injection can cause real harm. Their analysis found that 36.4 percent of OpenClaw's built-in skills pose high or critical risks. SafeClaw-R enforces safety as a system-level invariant over the execution graph. Actions are mediated before they run, and skills gain safe twins. Tests gave 95.2 percent accuracy in Google Workspace scenarios and detected 97.8 percent of malicious skill patterns.
arxiv-2603-29007: Yasui and co-authors present JWST's first mid-infrared census of protoplanetary disks in a low-metallicity region. They observed Digel Cloud 2, a star forming region in the outer Galaxy with two young clusters. Imaging from 1 to 20 microns probes disks with spatial detail and low stellar mass limits. About 75 percent of sources in both clusters retain thick disks. That rate matches solar-metallicity regions of like age. A lack of 2 micron excess hints at weaker inner disk emission. Accretion signatures appear in about 35 percent of sources, at high rates.
arxiv-2603-29107: Marini and co-authors design a hardware platform for testing single cells inside battery modules. Studying cells inside a full pack is hard without taking the pack apart. Their platform was built for the Audi e-tron battery pack. It combines voltage sensors, balancing circuits, and a microcontroller. The team screened cells across all 36 modules of the pack. Cell voltages were held to a set reference value. The platform supports safe health checks and later pack reuse.
arxiv-2603-29207: Tian and co-authors present TORCH, a framework for measuring route filtering in IPv6. RPKI validation should block invalid route origins and slow prefix hijacks. Its real protective effect in IPv6 is poorly measured. TORCH reuses open tunnel endpoints as global vantage points. A cross-plane inference trick judges reachability without responsive targets. The team finds about 27 percent of networks have near-full protection. Some large permissive networks still transit traffic toward invalid origins.
arxiv-2603-29307: Thomas and co-authors test a rotating frame used in waveform models of merging binaries. The frame tracks the main emission direction and should strip out precession effects. The open question is whether it still helps when orbits are eccentric. The team used 20 full numerical simulations with both spin precession and eccentricity. They compared waveforms in the fixed frame and the rotating frame. Errors fell in the rotating frame, but stayed too high for precise work. The frame did help surrogate models reach lower errors.
arxiv-2603-29507: Moretti and co-authors present a two-stage method for clearing haze from nighttime images. Night haze cuts visibility, warps color, and lowers contrast. Uneven artificial light makes the task harder. Stage one corrects the transmittance map with region-aware tweaks. It also estimates the air light map in the YUV color space. Stage two splits the image into structure and texture layers. The structure layer gets light and color fixes. The texture layer gets detail sharpening. A two-phase fusion then blends the layers.
arxiv-2603-30007: Zhang and co-authors build a neural Riemann solver with hard built-in constraints. Godunov methods need fluxes from local Riemann problems at cell faces. Exact solvers are faithful but slow, so practice leans on rough approximations. Weakly trained networks can break balance, symmetry, and conservation. Their solver enforces positivity, consistency, mirror symmetry, and two invariances. On shallow water and Euler tests, it matches the exact solver closely. An unconstrained twin loses symmetry and smears key jets.
arxiv-2604-00007: Kim and team present Dynin-Omni, the first masked-diffusion omnimodal model joining text, image, and speech tasks, plus video tasks, in one design. Unlike older models that order heterogeneous modes, or compositional models needing external decoders, Dynin-Omni treats modelling as masked diffusion over shared discrete tokens, allowing iterative refinement with bidirectional context. It trains in multiple stages, with model-merging expansion and cross-modal alignment. Across 19 multimodal benchmarks, it achieves 87.6 on GSM8K, beating existing open-source unified models while staying close to strong expert tools.
arxiv-2604-00207: Buckley and three colleagues apply a reservoir device, an unpoled cube of lead zirconate titanate, to digit sorting. The device reaches an 89.0 percent score on MNIST handwritten digits, about 2 points above logistic regression baselines on the same prepared data. On AudioMNIST spoken digits it matches the baseline at about 88 percent, which suggests such devices help most at intermediate difficulty. They shine where tasks beat simple linear models yet stay doable, and the substance already serves in semiconductor uses at low power.
arxiv-2604-00307: Erdinc and four colleagues introduce SAGE, a framework for statistically sound proxy velocities from sparse well logs and migrated seismic images. Training builds a proxy posterior over models from both inputs. At inference, SAGE produces full-detail fields from migrated images alone, with well data in the learned distribution. Tested on synthetic and field data, it captures subsurface variety under limited data, and its samples can train downstream networks for inversion workflows.
arxiv-2604-00507: Park and colleagues introduce RegFormer for weakly supervised human-object interaction detection. The task learns interactions from image-level labels alone, which helps machines read scenes. Older setups first run an outside tool to propose pairs, then reason over those pairs. That approach grows costly as pairs grow in number, and pairs that never act together trigger false alarms. RegFormer grounds relations straight, giving fast and exact pair work under image-level labels only.
arxiv-2604-00607: Goh and colleagues improve bounds for the binary paint shop problem, an APX-hard task. With n car models, each appearing twice in a 2n-long sequence, the goal is a colouring where each pair is painted differently while minimising paint swaps along it. A heuristic, recursive star greedy, is conjectured to reach a swap ratio of 0.361, beating quantum approximate optimisation at depth 7. Its average swap ratio caps the problem, since logarithmic-depth quantum performance is instance-independent. The authors extend the quantum method to depth 17, tightening that bound.
arxiv-2604-00707: Goodwin and colleagues study particle motion in choppy superfluid helium-4 down to the zero-temperature limit. An injection system for particles, 1 to 6 microns across, was built to see flows in helium-4 down to 0.14 K. Sound bursts launch them into the sample, and they descend under gravity, imaged by glow in a light sheet. The team reports number patterns during descent, including smooth and erratic paths showing contacts with thermal excited states and vortex lines. Speed patterns across temperatures prove Gaussian, with heavy tails that persist to zero temperature.
arxiv-2604-01307: Bibbens, Borevitz and McCauley tackle text indexing with mismatches: preprocess a string so queries find substrings within Hamming distance k. Prior best bounds come from the CGL tree, but high space may not be needed. They give a linear-space data structure whose query time drops alphabet dependence. For linear space it is the best known query time when k is at least 3. They also give the first sublinear-space results, using only o(n) space via function inversion on the CGL tree.
arxiv-2604-01407: Su and colleagues treat gravitational-wave emission from gravitational atoms, clouds of very light bosons around black holes from superradiance. For systems, they derive strain terms for transition and annihilation channels. For pairs, they model driven level shifts with Landau-Zener method, finding signals. Binary-driven ones yield signals with durations matching response times. But their strain lies well below limits at distances, and event rates suppress detectability by requiring separations. They quantify sensitivity, bandwidth and response gains, identifying these atoms around primordial black holes as a target for searches.
arxiv-2604-01507: Roldan proves the quantum walk characteristic polynomial determines a strongly regular graph of prime order up to isomorphism. First, the walk operator splits into blocks under the discrete Fourier transform. Second, a formula recovers each Fourier coefficient from an eigenvalue distinct from plus and minus one. Third, the inverse Fourier transform recovers the connection set. Graph isomorphism for such graphs is thus decidable in polynomial time using the quantum walk spectrum.
arxiv-2604-01607: Lyu presents ModTrans, a tool turning any real-world model to ASTRA-sim input, ending the barrier between machine learning experts and system teams. Large-scale shared training is a hot topic, but tests without real gear and kit are hard. Current sims like ASTRA-sim cannot import real-world built models, posing hurdles for teams seeking to use them. Tests show ModTrans's cost is tiny.
arxiv-2604-01907: Chen and colleagues turn unlabeled web video into training data for machines grasping 3D scenes. Labeled 3D data is scarce and costly, while raw video is plentiful, so the team built data engines generating training sets and studied what makes learning from them work. They tested it from low-level jobs, object spotting and outlining, up to reasoning jobs, spatial question answering and navigation. Models trained on the generated data performed strongly without tuning and improved further after tuning, showing web video sharpens scene understanding.
arxiv-2604-02007: Pardinas and team train Apriel-Reasoner, an open weight model, with a multi domain reinforcement learning recipe using public data. Training is hard because length, difficulty and efficiency vary across domains. Their recipe covers mathematics, code, instructions, puzzles and function calling. Sampling preserves ratios, and a difficulty aware penalty lengthens hard reasoning and shortens easy reasoning. Under a 16K budget, it works at 32K and beats its base model on AIME 2025, GPQA, MMLU-Pro and LiveCodeBench. It produces 30 to 50 percent shorter traces with the best accuracy tradeoff.
arxiv-2604-02107: Pang, Zhou, Chen and Wei fuse sparse visual odometry with a feed forward mapping model into one hybrid tracker. Their HyVGGT-VO frontend switches adaptively between optical flow and the VGGT model, while a hierarchical optimizer jointly refines poses and prediction scale for global consistency. Against VGGT-SLAM 2.0 it cuts average trajectory error by about 91 percent on EuRoC MAV and 20 percent on TUM RGB-D, running at 16.1 Hz pose output on a laptop GPU.
arxiv-2604-02307: Chen and colleagues build a quantum Monte Carlo route to symmetry resolved entanglement in lattice systems. Measuring disorder operators in plain and replica sets, they rebuild sector Renyi entropies from charged moments. Tests on the transverse field Ising model, where exact field theory results exist, and the Heisenberg chain validate the method. Applied to the two dimensional Ising model, the data support equal sharing of entanglement at the critical point.
arxiv-2604-03207: McKinnon and colleagues test whether comet hypervolatiles form when light splits other ices, rather than by trapping at formation. They shine ultraviolet light and fire electrons at ice analogs made from carbon dioxide, ammonia, and water mixes, and find carbon monoxide and nitrogen in every treated ice. Almost all observed cometary nitrogen fits this light-driven route, while most carbon monoxide still points to low-temperature trapping.
arxiv-2604-03307: Zhou and colleagues turn multimodal models from passive watchers into active questioners of images. Their V-Reflection method lets hidden reasoning states probe visual features for task-critical evidence, guided first by a box-guided teacher and then distilled into a dynamic student. At run time both helper modules stay off, keeping decoding purely autoregressive, and tests across six benchmarks narrow the fine-grained perception gap.
arxiv-2604-03507: Dogan and colleagues build machine-learning models that predict magnetic flux changes during solar active region emergence from brightness and solar wave power maps. Their simpler MagFluxLSTM beats the more complex MagFluxEnc-Dec encoder-decoder: among the top 100 tuning settings, 98 percent use MagFluxLSTM. The simpler model predicts flux rise 3 to 10 hours ahead within a 12-hour window for five test regions.
arxiv-2604-03607: Pavlov and colleagues examined how twisted light, photons carrying orbital angular momentum, interacts with atoms treated as localized wave packets. In head-on hits with a small offset, the photon handed nearly all of its twist to the atom's motion, while larger offsets shifted the average twist. The team also predicted a sideways atomic recoil near the light vortex, an effect within reach of cold-beam and trap experiments.
arxiv-2604-03707: Thijs de Kok asked whether every space that admits a Lorentzian metric also admits one whose Weyl curvature is purely electric or purely magnetic. He showed that certain products of Pontryagin forms must vanish when the curvature is even or odd under orientation reversal. That vanishing blocks such metrics on some compact spaces. The blocks also speak to Petrov types, which sort exact solutions of Einstein's equations, and to foliations by umbilic hypersurfaces.
arxiv-2604-03907: Jaewon Yoo and colleagues asked whether intracluster light can tell self-interacting dark matter from cold dark matter. They re-ran Cluster-EAGLE clusters from identical starting conditions under both models and compared dark matter shapes with gas, stars, galaxies, and brightest-cluster-galaxy-plus-ICL. The BCG-plus-ICL light traced dark matter best, staying robust at high redshift, while gas started poor and improved over time. In the self-interacting case, gas resembled dark matter more closely, as collisions made dark matter behave more like gas.
arxiv-2604-04207: Suresh Raghu and Satwik Pandey found that reasoning vision-language models grow more accurate while steadily losing visual grounding as they think. Across three models on MathVista, HallusionBench, and MMMU_Pro, attention to marked evidence regions fell sharply, often losing over half the evidence mass. Full-response entropy proved the most reliable text-only uncertainty signal across datasets, while adding vision features with one global linear rule proved brittle. A targeted vision veto cut selective risk by up to 1.9 percentage points at 90 percent coverage on sustained visual-reference tasks.
arxiv-2604-04307: Vaithilingam and colleagues present MagicCopy, an AI helper that moves data across apps while preserving its shape and styling. Copy-and-paste breaks down when apps use different table formats, forcing users to rebuild structure and reformat colours by hand. MagicCopy reads source and target context plus plain-language user instructions, then extracts, parses, transforms and reformats data automatically. In a study with sixteen people moving data across three pairs of tools, users picked it up quickly and found further uses for smoother cross-app work.
arxiv-2604-04407: Nasir, Liu and Mian present NAIMA, a guided depth super-resolution framework restoring fine structure from low-resolution depth plus high-resolution colour. Colour and texture cues in the colour image often mislead, blurring depth boundaries. NAIMA instead injects semantic priors from pretrained vision transformer tokens straight into the depth branch. Its Guided Token Attention module lets depth encodings query semantic tokens from deeper layers, gated to admit evidence only as it cuts reconstruction error. Alignment emerges implicitly under one reconstruction loss, and NAIMA leads on cross-dataset generalization.
arxiv-2604-04507: Kumar and colleagues present DHFP-PE, a dual-precision float processing element for AI speed-up, with FP8 and FP4 formats for low-power, high-throughput workloads. A bit-splitting technique lets a single 4-bit multiplier work either as a standard 4x4 multiplier for FP8 or as twin 2x2 multipliers for 2-bit inputs. It avoids copied logic. Built in 28 nm technology, the element reaches up to 60.4 percent area cut and large power savings against current designs. It suits energy-tight AI use and mixed-precision computing in accelerator chips.
arxiv-2604-04607: Liu, Schülke and Zhang determine the asymptotics of maximum F-bootstrap percolation running time for a large class of k-graphs. In the F-process starting from H0, each step adds edges completing a new copy of F. Running time is the smallest step where nothing changes. The k-extension of a graph G enlarges each edge with k minus 2 new vertices. For every t-vertex graph G and every k at or above 3, the running time stays below a constant depending on t and k.
arxiv-2604-04707: DataFlow Team and 41 colleagues offer OpenWorldLib, a shared inference framework for Advanced World Models. World models draw notice in artificial intelligence, yet a unified definition is lacking. The team defines a world model as a sight-centered model or framework with interaction and long-term memory, for grasping and predicting the complex world. The paper lists world model capabilities. Built on this definition, OpenWorldLib joins models across tasks, enabling easy reuse and joint inference. The paper closes with notes on future world model research.
arxiv-2604-04807: Feng, Wang, and Zhou improve regression for data where predictors carry measurement error and responses show heavy tails, a setting where a 2026 principal-components estimator loses stability. They swap its squared loss for a Wilcoxon rank loss, then add one adaptive reweighting step to curb shrinkage bias from the first fit. Their theorem bounds prediction for the second-stage fitted mean, and simulations show steady gains under heavy-tailed errors, especially when predictors are contaminated.
arxiv-2604-05207: Park and four colleagues show that plasmons on a surface with chiral flows tell mirror twins apart better than chiral boxes. A treatment uses charge and magnet moments. A chiral plasmon's telling factor can exceed the best box's by almost tenfold, due to stronger field trapping. Plasmons couple to a charge shadow onto a whole plane, while boxes couple only to one spin axis, giving a √2 boost. A mirror further lifts the gain, opening a route to chiral sensing with twisted-layer platforms.
arxiv-2604-05307: Ito and Hirano ask how far hot quark matter in high-energy oxygen-oxygen collisions settles into local balance. Their core-corona picture tracks both a settled fluid core and unsettled corona particles. Once charged particles near the centre pass about 20, the core outweighs the corona. Yet corona particles still matter even in head-on collisions, and strange baryon ratios stay below full chemical balance, so pure fluid models miss part of the physics.
arxiv-2604-05407: Kim and five colleagues reframe code agents around a structured action space of named syntax-tree entities instead of raw text spans, whose brittle string matching often fails. Their CODESTRUCT tools fetch whole syntactic units and apply syntax-checked edits to program elements. Across six models on SWE-Bench Verified, accuracy rises while token use falls, and GPT-5-nano improves by about 21 percent as empty-patch failures drop sharply.
arxiv-2604-05507: Liu, Pei, and Zhu trace how anime characters evolved over decades from a large review-site dataset of text, images, and production traits. They find audiences shifted from children toward teens and young adults, designs grew softer and more sexualized in female traits since the 2000s, and visual cues outweigh personality in driving popularity. Some archetypes prove visually predictable, yet audiences still favor less conventional characters.
arxiv-2604-05707: Homeyer and four colleagues hunt breath markers of fat burning beyond acetone, which only shifts hours after exercise. Nineteen volunteers cycled twice while breath was scanned by mass spectrometry against blood ketone readings. Of 773 candidate signals, only four tracked the reference, all acetone-related, and end-of-exercise readings predicted large post-exercise shifts well. No new marker emerged, confirming acetone's lead role.
arxiv-2604-05907: A-thano and twenty-three colleagues sharpen hot Jupiter WASP-43 b with 35 new transit light curves plus old and space data. Study of 188 mid-transit times finds no clear orbital decay. Atmosphere fits tie hotter fits to more water, but mixed tools muddy the read, so the team calls for sharper future data sets.
arxiv-2604-06007: Danil Vyskubov and three colleagues test how hybrid quantum-classical classifiers scale. They ask how accuracy and quantum behaviour change as circuit depth and qubit count grow. Their 2026 paper varies layers at fixed qubit count and qubits at fixed depth across several datasets. It tracks accuracy, precision, recall, and quantum measures. The results map where gains level off and how results shift by dataset. That gives practical guidance for choosing depth and qubit count in such classifiers.
arxiv-2604-06107: Barkeshli, Douglas, and Freedman ask how AI might open a grand view of mathematics beyond logic. Their 2026 essay sketches the formal structure of mathematics through universal proof and structural hypergraphs, raising basic questions. It then lists the parts and criteria for AI models capable of automated mathematical discovery. As AI agents traverse Platonic mathematical worlds, the authors expect lessons about mathematics as a whole and its small ribbons for human minds. The essay closes on the old question: is mathematics found or made?
arxiv-2604-06407: He and Zhang tackle mediation-analysis positivity violations for antigen-experienced people. Controlled effects estimate risk curves with all vaccinated and levels fixed. That setup works for antigen-naïve groups but breaks when prior shots or infection shapes immunity, as with influenza, dengue, and COVID-19. The violation bites because no plausible intervention sets a marker below baseline. Their weighted controlled risk approach targets the subpopulation with a prespecified chance of reaching that level, generalizing to contrasts. Simulations support it, and it reanalyzes Omicron antibody titers in the COVAIL trial.
arxiv-2604-06507: Rahman fine-tunes Whisper for Pashto, missing from its pre-training. Off-the-shelf models print Arabic, Dari, or Urdu script for Pashto audio above 100 percent error. Vanilla fine-tuning wins at 21.22 percent on whisper-base, beating LoRA, frozen-encoder, and Urdu transfer. Frozen-encoder tuning degrades the model; Urdu transfer fails on an unverified checkpoint, mismatch, and thin training. On newer data, whisper-small reaches about 25 percent and large-turbo about 23 percent, making small optimal. Augmentation adds about 7 points; analysis finds suffix confusion and retroflex substitutions dominant.
arxiv-2604-06807: Seto runs the first test of the hybrid ring strategy for interstellar signaling. The scheme, a Schelling-point plan for interstellar signaling, anchors on bright GRB 221009A plus the measured distance to the Galactic center. That pairing ties sky position to a tight arrival window, and TESS watched the region for about 50 days in 2024. Among 58 stars, two showed brightenings inside predicted windows, but both matched nearby-star excursions, pointing to instrumental origins. The test shows the strategy works with survey data and promises a basis for future technosignature searches.
arxiv-2604-07107: Lingua and three colleagues show in the lab how to build two dimensional continuous variable cluster states from microwave modes. Cluster states are linked quantum states that can serve as a base for quantum computing, and the team built them across one hundred ninety one microwave modes. Vacuum wobble fed into a Josephson parametric amplifier, pumped by tones near twice its natural pitch, yields honeycomb and square grids. A nullifier test proves the clusters are present, with clear squeezing of the cluster checks.
arxiv-2604-07307: Nairn improves approximate full mass matrix methods, known as FMPM(k), for material point method simulations. These methods sharpen grid velocities computed from grid momentum and can be added to any MPM code as a new task wherever velocities are needed. The recommended implementation runs only once per time step, just before particle positions and velocities update. Nairn then revises the FMPM loop so it plays well with lumped-mass features like boundary conditions, multimaterial contact, and crack contact, and he analyzes stability and cost versus order.
arxiv-2604-07507: Cuevas-Pacheco, Riffo, and Emery propose a LASSO-penalized method for multivariate spatial Gaussian fields, where counts explode and likelihood work is costly. Since not all cross-links matter, sparse covariance structures are attractive. Their method sparsifies the Cholesky factor of the Matérn correlation matrix, finding uncorrelated variable pairs and keeping it valid. A block descent algorithm splits optimization into small tasks with constraints enforced. Simulations recover sparse structures and cut error, and a geochemical case with 36 variables and 3998 locations makes spatial prediction feasible where others fail.
arxiv-2604-08707: Kučera and Martinek extend Courcelle's theorem from checking graph properties to representing models of monadic second order formulas. Models with free variables can be captured by a decision diagram sized in a parameterized linear way by treewidth and formula size. In particular, sentential decision diagrams stay parameterized linear in treewidth, and ordered binary decision diagrams in pathwidth. Yet some bounded treewidth graph class admits no treewidth parameterized ordered binary diagram, a limit proved from Razgon's lower bound.
arxiv-2604-09607: Dehury and four colleagues address edge analytics that stay hard-coded until engineers rewrite and redeploy scripts. Their LEI framework lets a cloud-hosted language model coordinate device-side logic as conditions change, removing manual business rules. Candidate programs are generated and checked against data and constraints. The winner is deployed to each device, tailored by sample data, metadata, and resource limits. Tests on four datasets show low processor and memory use while adapting to change: air quality, temperature and humidity, wind, and soil.
arxiv-2604-10007: Lakzian maps smooth compact Ricci flows using only metrics and sizes, with one case needing good scalar bend along the flow. The forms weakly define super Ricci flows and impose a fullness rule, stated only in metric and measure terms, forcing the super Ricci flow gap to hold as match. These weak forms extend easily to the rough setting.
arxiv-2604-10307: Espejo and three colleagues launch the Asymmetric Hub Location Problem, where origins and targets connect under share limits. Current models assume even shares, but real uses need one-sided handling. The team focuses on the (1,p) variant, with single-linked origins and multi-linked targets, for relief aid and supply chains. They propose two integer forms: a four-index take and a three-index form. The version shrinks size and lifts power.
arxiv-2604-10407: Ghosh and Pramanik predict finger width in a tapered Hele-Shaw cell by pure math. A steady depth slope bends the classic finger choice rule, which their perturbation method captures. Their formula ties width shift to the gap slope and the modified capillary number. At zero slope, the rule falls back to the known parallel cell result. Tests match lab widths well, and the slope sign can steady or upset the single finger state.
arxiv-2604-10607: Hamid extends a physics-informed fix for the barren-plateau problem in variational quantum algorithms, where gradients vanish and training stalls. His adaptive method widens the reachable quantum states along a guarded trajectory that keeps gradient variance from collapsing, with a proven safety bound on the expansion rate. Across 16 benchmarks with up to 14 qubits it doubles the fidelity of the static version, reaching 0.54 against 0.27, and it finds the negative ground state of a Heisenberg chain model where static methods fail.
arxiv-2604-11707: Karypidis, Gidaris, and Komodakis present Re2Pix, a two-stage video forecast tool that predicts scene meaning before pixels. Rather than RGB frames, it first forecasts scene structure in a frozen vision foundation model's space. It then feeds those representations to a latent diffusion model to render realistic frames. Two training strategies, nested dropout and mixed guidance, counter train-test mismatch between ground-truth and forecast representations. On driving benchmarks, the meaning-first design improves temporal meaning consistency, image appeal, and training speed over strong diffusion baselines.
arxiv-2604-12307: Xia and six colleagues propose LoRA-based pairwise training to keep AI-generated image detectors robust under severe real-world distortions. Their plan fine-tunes a visual foundation model, mimics distortion and size shifts to match test data, and splits generalization from robustness tuning through pairwise training. The approach placed in the NTIRE robust detection challenge.
arxiv-2604-12407: Gregory Morse and Tamás Kozsik argue that self-modifying code can serve as tamper protection. Such programs rewrite their own instructions while running. Theory says non-modifying code can simulate them on an idealized machine. Real processors add timing, ordering, and hardware state as observables. A faithful fake then grows detectably costly, the authors argue. Their model joins introspective and shape-shifting code with reliable clocks and timing checks. Careful engineering keeps overhead low while preserving detection.
arxiv-2604-12607: Rhyan Barrett and two colleagues design multi-part chemical systems. Catalysts and enzymes work through interplay of parts, not lone molecules. Brute-force search over mixes and layouts is infeasible. Their plan pairs a genetic search with a generative molecule model. Shape and mix refine in a closed loop. A test case builds catalytic surroundings for a Claisen rearrangement. Checks show a 30 percent cut in activation barrier. The plan extends to catalysts, enzyme sites, and new materials.
arxiv-2604-12907: Thea Budde and two colleagues show generalized symmetries can fragment Hilbert space. That means vastly many split Krylov sectors as systems grow. Ordinary symmetries yield at most a tame count. Higher-form, subsystem, and gauge symmetries yield vastly many sectors. Other symmetries split further within single sectors. Many known models fragment this way, so many Krylov sectors alone do not prove ergodicity breaking. Clean localization follows from Krylov-limited settling without translation invariance.
arxiv-2604-13107: Ivanov, Rana, and Prabhakaran ask whether coding agents can handle general business work, testing one agent on practical tasks in an open-core enterprise resource planning system. The agent reliably completes simple tasks but fails characteristically on complex ones, where bridging domain logic and code execution proves the key bottleneck. The study exposes gaps in current evaluations, which rarely probe end-to-end business process automation beyond software engineering.
arxiv-2604-13307: Buranasiri and Murphy group hyperspectral images with no labels, using images that record many spectral bands per pixel. A masked autoencoder with a Vision Transformer backbone first learns a clean latent view using only a small subset of pixels. Superpixels from the entropy-rate algorithm then support a diffusion graph with spatial rules in that compressed space. Their DS2DL method improves labeling accuracy and clustering quality on the Botswana and KSC datasets.
arxiv-2604-13407: Rongzong Huang, Jiayi Huang, and Qing Li improve the third-order scheme in the pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann model for multiphase flows. They analyse two-phase Poiseuille flow discretely, deriving a velocity equation for grid-aligned and grid-oblique cases. That analysis pinpoints the terms behind spurious velocity oscillations near phase interfaces. Their improved scheme suppresses those oscillations with no added complexity. Tests on Poiseuille flow, annular shear flow, and a falling droplet confirm it. In the droplet case, oscillations would overstate drag.
arxiv-2604-13607: Kruse and Seifert study families of operators on a broad class of spaces. The families vary continuously in the strong sense and stay equicontinuous locally. For Saks spaces, they link these ideas to bi-continuity and equitightness. That link recovers known results for bi-continuous semigroups and cosine families. It also extends those results to the broader setting.
arxiv-2604-14007: Sim and Choo talk to peer supporters about emotional labour, responsibility, and AI. Lived experience, moral duty, and self-image shape who takes part. Fuzzy rules leave boundary calls and hand-offs to single people. They judge AI less by feeling or skill than by how it shifts risk, labour, and accountability, pointing design toward duty first.
arxiv-2604-14507: Huang, Ji, Duan, and Ye propose H2VLR, a heterogeneous hypergraph system for few-shot anomaly detection with vision-language models. Current schemes infer anomalies almost entirely by pairwise feature matching, ignoring structure and global fit. H2VLR instead treats the task as high-order judgments over visual-semantic relations, modeling regions and concepts jointly in one hypergraph. Tests on industrial and medical benchmarks often reach the top, and the team promises code on acceptance.
arxiv-2604-15007: Iyer gives a counter-example to persistence in generalised preferential attachment trees. In such a tree, each new node connects to an existing node with probability proportional to a function of its degree. The author had conjectured that if the sum of inverse squares of the attachment function converges, a persistent hub exists: one node holding maximal degree for all but finitely many time-steps. His counter-example, a minor modification of one by Galganov and Ilienko, disproves the conjecture.
arxiv-2604-15107: Zheng and Raskutti address feature picking with MinShap, a Shapley-based tool built for redundancy. A feature can earn a positive Shapley score yet add nothing once other variables are known, so averaging scores misleads. MinShap instead takes the smallest contribution across conditioning sets, testing whether a feature stays useful in every context. Under a simple null monotonicity condition, this smallest value exactly marks redundant features and yields a sound picking rule.
arxiv-2604-15307: Kasai hunts certified caps for the minimum distance of a family of quantum LDPC codes built from affine permutation matrices, all with girth-eight Tanner graphs. Rather than proving a general lower bound, he constructs low-weight logical representatives and certifies them by kernel and row-space exclusion tests. The search sharpens earlier upper bounds and yields concrete certified values, with an exactness criterion for the block-compression case.
arxiv-2604-15407: Dark and four colleagues build SHIELD, a gas-driven rig that measures hydrogen movement through structural materials for fusion devices.
