arxiv-2605-13207: Stojanovic and Proutiere extend successor measures so hierarchy can guide zero shot reinforcement learning. Older hierarchical methods lean on fixed time spans or goal only tasks, limiting them to narrow reward settings. Their switching measures yield both a high level choice policy and a low level control policy from one learned form. Tests on goal tasks and general reward tasks beat flat baselines and match top hierarchical methods on goal tasks.
arxiv-2605-13307: Hannah Rose Kirk and six colleagues re-recruit 530 participants from 52 countries to test personalised language models. The participants had given their preferences to the PRISM dataset two years earlier. Preference fine-tuning with P-DPO beats a generic model and personalised prompting. Adapting to one person's data adds little over training on pooled preferences from a diverse group. Fine-tuning also amplifies sycophancy that people reward in short tests. Simulated users recover broad rankings but not individual judgements.
arxiv-2605-13407: Namhyoung Kim and Jae Wook Song introduce PRISM-VQ, a dynamic factor framework for ranking stocks by predicted returns. Classical factor models are interpretable but rigid. Their model combines expert prior factors with discrete latent factors learned by vector quantisation. Vector quantisation compresses cross-sectional structure into codes and acts as a noise-suppressing bottleneck. A mixture-of-experts layer then supplies loadings that vary over time. Tests on the CSI 300 and S and P 500 show gains over strong baselines.
arxiv-2605-13607: Ihor Kendiukhov presents ergodicity, an open-source Python toolkit for computational work on stochastic dynamics. The package joins three layers often split across ad hoc scripts: process specs and simulators, plus analysis and fitting tools, and agent-based tests. It stresses non-ergodicity, time-average ways, heavy-tailed flows, and decision making under uncertainty. The article covers the software rather than new theory, with worked examples from heavy-tailed spread to partial stochastic differential equation work.
arxiv-2605-13907: Zhou and four colleagues tackle a mismatch in quantized reinforcement learning for language models, where low-precision rollouts feed a higher-precision trainer. The mismatch biases the policy gradient and can collapse training on reasoning tasks, though early on it also supplies a useful exploration bonus. Their Adaptive Importance Sampling method corrects the bias, tuning the strength of its intervention batch by batch as training proceeds.
arxiv-2605-14007: Sharma and Velusamy study non-redundancy for low-arity symmetric Boolean constraint problems. Non-redundancy means the largest size of a problem instance with no smaller sub-instance sharing its satisfying assignments. It steers kernelization, exact and approximate sparsification, and exact streaming cost. For Boolean symmetric problems set by an r-ary relation whose value hinges only on Hamming weight, the paper gives a near-full classification of how non-redundancy grows.
arxiv-2605-14107: Shah and four co-authors study the surface linear photogalvanic effect in the magnetic Weyl semimetal Co3Sn2S2. The effect dies out in the centrosymmetric bulk but is allowed on the surface, where inversion symmetry breaks. Unitary crystal symmetries on the surface flip the sign of the total photocurrent at certain polarization angles when magnetization flips. An antiunitary mirror symmetry tightly constrains the intrinsic share, forcing several nonlinear response tensor parts to zero, while the extrinsic share escapes those limits and runs large.
arxiv-2605-14407: Xiang Li argues the key AI capability boundary lies inside digital work, not between digital and hands-on tasks. He names that middle zone Metis AI, after metis, Greek hands-on contextual knowledge, for screen tasks defying machine handling. Such tasks are tangled in rules, social ties and norms, not hard to compute. He splits metis into constitutive kinds, lost when spelled out, and operational kinds, taken in by machines. Traits follow, from consequential irreversibility to accountability anchoring. His response is centaur systems where humans lead and AI supports.
arxiv-2605-14607: Li and Wang argue that most video models grasp literal content but miss subtext such as metaphor, irony and social meaning. Their ViMU benchmark is the first designed to test whether frontier video models can read the implicit ideas and intentions creators convey through context, style and social experience. It probes understanding beyond objects, actions and temporal relations, where meanings can also shift across cultures and social groups.
arxiv-2605-14707: Alkac shows that, in the Kerr-Schild double copy, the thermodynamic Smarr formula for static spherically symmetric black holes matches the single-copy Gauss law in structure. Static black hole solutions of general relativity map to purely electric Maxwell solutions in flat spacetime under this copy. Extending the argument to asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetimes, the pressure-volume term is proved to emerge from a gauge-theoretic background subtraction. This links the double copy to black hole thermodynamics.
arxiv-2605-14907: Yisen Gao and seven colleagues present KGPFN, a foundation model for knowledge graphs that reasons about new entities and relations it has never seen. It learns relation patterns by passing messages across relation graphs, then draws on local neighborhood context and global examples of the query relation at run time. No parameter updates are needed during inference. Across 57 knowledge graphs it reached the best average ranking score with and without fine-tuning.
arxiv-2605-15107: George E. Andrews and Mohamed El Bachraoui answer two Hecke-sum questions posed by Banerjee and Bringmann. The pair had proved a conjectured Hecke-type identity for a two-color partition series with modular methods. They asked for a direct Bailey-pair proof, plus an investigation of the series' odd part. Applying Bailey's transform to an Andrews Bailey pair and a Lovejoy conjugate pair, the authors give formulas for both even and odd parts. The original conjecture is the specialization at a equals 1.
arxiv-2605-15207: Yi Xie and five others spot a structural failure in fine-tuning multi-agent language-model teams. Retraining one agent shifts the shared context, and evaluating later updates on cached rollouts compounds the mismatch. They frame this compounding occupancy shift, proving stale-presence scoring incurs a penalty growing fast with agent count, versus linear for middle-presence scoring. Their TeamTR framework redraws trajectories after each update with per-agent trust regions. It yields improvement lower bounds and beats single-agent and stepwise baselines by 7.1 percent on average.
arxiv-2605-15507: Bumsu Park, Chanho Park, Youngmok Park, and Namyoon Lee build a rate-distortion theory for Gaussian-mixture sources. One spread matrix cannot catch their varied local shapes. Their key find: the mix costs only its part label. One shared waterfilling level then steers bit shares across parts and modes. Their PrismQuant sends the label with no loss. It codes each rest with its matched transform, then scalar steps. It nears the theory bound on toy data. On real wireless channel data it beats far larger learned codecs.
arxiv-2605-15707: Michael Hudler, Franz Thaler, and Martin Urschler test whether explicit shape priors help whole-heart CT segmentation. Standard convolutional nets do not enforce anatomical plausibility outright. The team tests shape-aware losses and heatmap-guided U-Net variants on two cardiac sets. Across all tests, a plain 3D U-Net stays a very strong baseline. Handcrafted priors give at best patchy, small gains and often hurt scores. The baseline seems to already capture implicit anatomical regularities. Future gains likely need richer learned priors, not simple handcrafted shape constraints.
arxiv-2605-15907: Jiaming Chen and Almut E. D. Veraart introduce Lévy-driven graph Ornstein-Uhlenbeck models for edge-indexed network time series. The framework extends network autoregressive processes to continuous time and adapts node-based graph dynamics to edges. It handles general Lévy noise, capturing both Brownian and jump behavior. The authors estimate parameters by maximum likelihood and derive the estimator's large-sample traits. Simulations test small samples, and a high-frequency finance application shows better forecasts and faster computation than standard benchmarks, with robustness from network design.
arxiv-2605-16007: Fujun He and fourteen colleagues build Ascend-RaBitQ, a system for billion-scale vector similarity search that splits work between neural processing units and CPUs. Coarse ranking runs on the NPU over 1-bit quantized vectors, while host CPUs re-rank finalists at full precision, breaking the usual accuracy-memory-speed trade-off. On standard datasets it builds indexes 3.0 to 62.8 times faster than a CPU baseline and reaches up to 11.7 times the throughput of the fastest CPU rival.
arxiv-2605-16607: Dobák and Mulrenin sharpen a classic bound for hypergraph Ramsey numbers, which concern how large a structure must grow before a set pattern is forced to appear. They extend the vertex online Ramsey game from graphs to hypergraphs and prove a tighter recurrence for it. The result improves the long-standing Erdős–Rado bound by a lower-order term and yields better quantitative limits for hypergraph Ramsey numbers.
arxiv-2605-16707: Jaiswal and colleagues propose an on-device, interpretable intrusion-detection system for Internet of Medical Things networks, built on Tsetlin Machines. The rule-driven model represents attack patterns in propositional logic and explains decisions through feature contributions, vote scores, and clause heatmaps. On the MedSec-25 dataset covering realistic attack phases, it reaches a macro F1 score of 97.83%, beating standard machine-learning models. Raspberry Pi deployment supports real-time on-device inference.
arxiv-2605-16907: Siriwardana's team analyzes movable antenna arrays: a linear array of fixed parts moving along a line. With a full, space-coherent model and steady placement, they give near-exact estimates to the upper tail of the signal-to-noise ratio spread for linked and free parts. They also derive a closed-form formula for the level crossing rate under linked parts with split 2D linkage. Tests confirm closeness and tightness of bounds. Movable arrays beat single fluid-antenna and fixed systems, with tighter spacing adding gains.
arxiv-2605-17607: Martin Bichler and Jan-Sebastian Hoehener study Bayesian Bertrand competition with private costs and piecewise-linear pricing. They prove Minty stability fails near equilibrium in the continuous game, and in fine piecewise-linear approximations with flat segments. A sum-of-squares frame builds global Lyapunov maps for the projected flow, and feasible positive-rate checks imply global stability. A proximal Lyapunov proof gives last-iterate settling under persistent noise and shrinking steps. The search covers 243 systems, returning feasible results throughout, including 111 with verified Minty failure.
arxiv-2605-18107: Titus Hilberdink's 2026 paper gives a fresh account of growth rates that sit between polynomial and exponential growth. To name such rates at all, he first widens the basic toolkit with a tower of Abel functions. With those in hand, polynomials and exponentials fall into back-to-back classes, and the paper charts the large gaps between classes. Those gaps show how much stays unknown in between, above all if the continuum hypothesis for classes holds.
arxiv-2605-18207: Davide Germani's 2026 paper settles the sign of the effective range for a class of single-channel local interactions. In exotic hadron work the sign serves as a test: negative values point to compact multiquark states, positive values to loosely bound hadronic molecules. Germani proves that for finite-range potentials with a repulsive inner core and an attractive outer tail, the effective range stays strictly positive whenever the scattering length exceeds the potential range. The result puts that phenomenological test on rigorous footing.
arxiv-2605-18307: Donghui Yang and three co-authors extend earlier work on degenerate parabolic equations, heat-like models whose diffusion can vanish. With a variable-splitting method, they derive a Lebeau-Robbiano spectral inequality for a new equation. They use it to prove null controllability, driving solutions to zero, with control acting on a measurable subset rather than an open one, in 2026.
arxiv-2605-18707: Breitkopf and three co-authors solve, in a May 2026 paper, relative majority in population protocols with k cubed states. Agents start with one of k opinions, and each must output the most supported color. Earlier bounds put state complexity between order k squared and order k to the seventh. Their CIRCLES protocol partitions agents into circular linked lists of decreasing sizes, with no two agents sharing a color in one circle. An extension solves relative majority, and a modified version ranks opinions with two times k to the fourth states.
arxiv-2605-18807: Asher Labovich, Benjamin Bradley, Vanessa Alexander, and Chaitanya Harsha design block-based double decoders, a transformer build that mixes two training styles. Their doubly causal block masks allow full loss supervision and fixed sequence packing. In scaling tests they beat encoder-decoders and nearly match decoder-only models, while shrinking stored key-value data and work per token by at least two thirds at inference. The design keeps prefill caching and other decoder-only speed tricks.
arxiv-2605-18907: Yinbo Yu and six colleagues scan neural networks for backdoors in about a millisecond per model, without clean samples or knowledge of trigger patterns. Existing defenses lean on activation anomalies or trigger reconstruction and take minutes or hours, while attacks can plant a backdoor in milliseconds. Their DFBScanner instead inspects final-layer parameters, where backdoor shifts leave a distinctive mark, and combines anomaly indicators into one Trojan score. On a benchmark of over five thousand backdoored models it catches 97.17 percent with a false-positive rate under one percent.
arxiv-2605-19007: James Sinclair and ten colleagues report first stratospheric propadiene and propene high in Jupiter north. In the north auroral zone, propadiene tops twelve sigma and propene tops seventeen sigma. At sixty two degrees north, propadiene runs about forty times past model forecasts and propene about twenty eight times past. Gain inside the auroral zone points to auroral heat and charged bits stirring chemistry, while propane stayed unseen.
arxiv-2605-19207: Sumanth Meenan Kanneti and Aryan Shah present a shrinking framework for brain tumour MRI sorting, aimed at low-resource clinics. It mixes quantization-aware training, teaching a compact student, and Float16 shrinking on a light backbone. Full checks are given for this flow, trained by transfer learning and shrunk via TensorFlow Lite, while other plans await future checks. The shrunk model reaches 82.37 percent correct against an 82.20 percent base mark, shrinking from 35.34 MB to 5.76 MB, a 6.14-times shrink with no real score loss, holding across all four groups.
arxiv-2605-19407: Mohri, Duchi and Hashimoto test a common pretraining habit in the setting where it matters most, plentiful compute paired with scarce data. Scaling runs for large models show that long training lets them absorb low-quality and distracting material without harm, and nominally poor material can even help. That result flips the usual rule: when compute is ample, skipping selection entirely beats selecting at all. Their point is aimed at the belief that only high-quality text belongs in pretraining.
arxiv-2605-19507: Hodgson and team link wobbles in radio positions of active galactic nuclei to gamma-ray brightness. The celestial reference frame rests on these nuclei, yet structural change shifts their apparent spots. Measuring core offsets at two radio bands against ICRF3 and comparing with Fermi-LAT gamma-ray fluxes within thirty days, 57 of 92 sources had enough overlap. About 90 percent show significant power-law correlations, but signs mix and can flip between bands. No single mechanism explains the pattern, and only five sources show tentative time-lag evidence.
arxiv-2605-19907: Bonilla and colleagues study heat and charge flow in a graphene sheet split by a gain or loss wall. The wall's mix of gain and loss breaks the usual flux rule and swaps it for a net gain or loss balance. Tuned gain lifts both flows, while loss trims heat flow more and gives the best thermoelectric score.
arxiv-2605-20107: Robert Jenkinson Alvarez argues isotropic regularization is no benign default. For known geometry, minimax and maximum-entropy covariance take closed form under an energy budget, and isotropy incurs a price. When downstream geometry is unknown, no covariance shape is canonical, and oracle marginals from one view do not identify the view-to-view coupling. Bias should shape the cross-view coupling, not a fixed encoder marginal. HamJEPA encodes views as phase states and predicts with a leapfrog map. HamJEPA beats SIGReg on CIFAR-100, with symplectic coupling driving the gain.
arxiv-2605-20207: Ryan Smith, Kyle Chin and Tamara Munzner present HealthTale, a patient-centric visual tool for health stories. Patients struggle to tell health histories under time pressure, and systems favour clinician data over patient narratives. HealthTale's design comes from discussions, narratives, interviews, and elicited stories, identifying how people tell their stories. It turns freeform narratives into timelines grouped by health concern and time, handling vague timing and out-of-order events. Tests with patients and clinicians find HealthTale aids recall, organization and self-advocacy, while helping clinicians grasp narratives.
arxiv-2605-20507: Harańczyk and ten co-workers describe procuring and purifying liquid argon for LEGEND-200. The experiment needs high-purity argon to tell signal from background, and the team fills its cryostat to 91 tonnes. A copper-catalyst and molecular-sieve purifier strips oxygen and water, lifting the scintillation triplet lifetime from about 0.9 to 1.3 microseconds. After filling, lifetime reads 1.16 microseconds, dented by nitrogen from a spoiled delivery, though monitors blocked a larger influx.
arxiv-2605-20607: Romeo Valentin and three colleagues build a safety case for a vision-based aircraft landing system under European guidance for learned systems. A model that can be trusted, they argue, must at least split what it sees into content and style. They train a vision transformer to find runway points and break its patch codes into plain parts. Content parts track runway shape, style parts track look, and the final head leans almost all on content.
arxiv-2605-20707: Zongqi Yu proves a limiting distribution and convergence rate for GL(3) Fourier coefficients. Heath-Brown showed that the normalized error term in the Pilz divisor problem has a distribution function. Yu proves the analogue for a self-dual GL(3) Hecke-Maass cusp form, showing that x to the power of minus one third times the summed coefficients has a distribution function. The paper also gives a quantitative rate at which the finite distributions approach that limit.
arxiv-2605-21007: Daojie Peng and four colleagues present LiteViLNet, a lightweight vision-LiDAR fusion net for road segmentation. That task matters for self-driving cars and mobile robots, where appearance and geometric cues must be handled under edge-computing limits. Old multi-modal methods often improve accuracy with large encoders or costly global interaction, limiting use on embedded platforms. LiteViLNet pairs a MobileNetV3 RGB encoder with a tiny 0.12-million-parameter geometry net and multi-scale fusion.
arxiv-2605-21207: Xiaoyu Zhou and colleagues present Peak-Guided Calibration, a tool to spot AI-made images. As generators improve, fine clues get swamped by strong image content, and tools that read only the whole image miss them. Their peak-sensitive method spotlights the sharpest local clues and uses them to tune the global call. They also add CommGen15, a test set from fifteen commercial models, on which the tool leads prior methods.
arxiv-2605-21407: Brooke Kotten and co-authors test whether the subgiant TOI-5882 shows lithium enrichment from planetary engulfment. Theory predicts subgiants in a narrow mass regime can retain lithium signatures from engulfment, and TOI-5882 hosts a massive brown dwarf companion able to perturb inner planets. Using spectrograph data, they measure a lithium width of seventy-five point three nine milli-angstroms and an abundance of two point four nine dex, and compare to sixty-one control subgiants.
arxiv-2605-21607: Talant Talipov studies minimal spheres and scalar curvature. In 1982, S.-T. Yau conjectured four distinct embedded minimal two-spheres exist in any manifold diffeomorphic to the three-sphere. Wang-Zhou settled it for Riemannian three-spheres with bumpy metrics or positive Ricci curvature, and he proves a quantitative version. With positive Ricci curvature and scalar curvature at least Lambda-zero greater than zero, four distinct embedded minimal two-spheres exist. Each has area at most twelve pi times i plus one over Lambda-zero.
arxiv-2605-21707: Asadulaev builds a market-making system that keeps the classic Avellaneda-Stoikov pricing structure but adapts it to shifting market regimes. The design separates what the market is doing from what the trader wants: market state picks a small set of pricing parameters, while recent rewards set a small objective vector. A forward map then turns that objective into optimal bid and ask quotes, letting quotes respond to regime change without rebuilding the model.
arxiv-2605-21807: Doeun Lee and co-authors introduce OGCaReBench, a retrieval benchmark for clinical questions that fall outside evidence-based guidelines. Guidelines cover studied diagnostic and treatment paths, but the long tail of real care escapes them, and medical models mostly memorize common guideline knowledge. Built from published case reports and validated by medical experts, the benchmark poses long-form, free-text clinical questions about rare cases. Even the best baseline answers only fifty-six percent correctly, while retrieved medical articles lift performance to eighty-two percent, showing evidence grounding matters.
arxiv-2605-21907: Gang Dai and co-authors propose RTS, a reward-guided method for scaling diffusion models at test time by steering the full denoising trajectory. Earlier methods only search preset noise candidates or explore the trajectory rigidly, so RTS finds key points where the denoising direction shifts. Tests on SD v3, FLUX, and Qwen-Image show GenEval gains of 20.7 percent, 15.6 percent, and 12.2 percent over baselines. Those key points cluster mainly in the middle stage, unlike the structure-sensitive early phase and the late attribute phase.
arxiv-2605-22007: Jewon Yeom and co-authors argue hallucination in large language models is a commitment failure, not missing knowledge. The usual view says a model errs when the right answer is absent at generation time and succeeds when it is present. Using a semantic notion of answer availability that pools token variants for the same concept, they test whether the correct concept is available before generation. Correct generations concentrate mass on one surface form, while hallucinations spread it across alternatives, and the same asymmetry shows in pre-generation hidden states.
arxiv-2605-22407: Durgesh and colleagues evaluate ELEPHANT, a filter in the Fink broker that flags hostless extragalactic transients in real time. The pipeline works from image stamps with minimal information, for fast spotting. From 877 flagged events between September 2023 and December 2025, 67 prove truly hostless, with no host galaxy in lists or old images. Another 51 link to visible hosts absent from lists and stamps. Overall score hits 0.84, mostly Type Ia supernovae, followed by Type I superluminous supernovae. ELEPHANT now also processes the Rubin alert stream.
arxiv-2605-22507: Moreno-Muñoz and team offer a method for making new data via stepped-time random control of mass transport. Using classic control results, the problem becomes a linear program whose dual values give the best value function and best control policy. A fast no-sim primal-dual method finds nearly best value functions and linked value-driven transport rules. Well-trained VDT rules give straight paths run quickly and safely, and easily add conditional making, label-free steering, and solo transfer. Tests show strong scores and good growth room.
arxiv-2605-22807: Benhaj, Sengupta, and Branciard ask how much decoherence, or dephasing, a quantum switch can survive before its causal order turns definite. For two-party processes, dephasing everything, or leaving only the future system untouched, makes the process causally separable. Yet if any other single system stays untouched, some processes keep indefinite causal order. The same pattern holds for multi-party circuits with quantum control.
arxiv-2605-23107: Alfaro and colleagues use 2460 HAWC transits to constrain the extragalactic background light through the blazar Mrk 421, which varies across timescales. Selecting high and low emission states, they report evidence of a spectral cutoff during high states. An exponential cutoff power law beats a power law at 3.8 sigma, with the cutoff at 13 plus or minus 3 TeV. From this they derive limits on the intensity of background light photons. The cutoff differs from the value expected from gamma-ray interactions with background photons, indicating it is intrinsic to the source.
arxiv-2605-23307: Jupiter's banded winds, including a fast prograde jet at the equator, motivate two rotating spherical-shell simulations by Matilsky and three colleagues. One run isolates the deep convective zone; the other lets rising flows overshoot into a stable surface weather layer. In both, mixing of potential vorticity first builds high-latitude jets, while deep columnar flows drive equatorial superrotation. Adding the weather layer shifts the wind pattern off the rotation axis, and weaker jets drift poleward or merge over very long times.
arxiv-2605-23407: Zhang and colleagues design GeoCycler, a training-time alignment method for building cyclic peptides, ring-shaped molecules prized as drugs for their stability and precise targeting. Closing the ring demands sparse, awkward geometric constraints that sampling-time guidance only nudges. GeoCycler instead rewards feasible closures during training, with a gated reward that shapes distances only once the right residue or linker types are in place. On the LNR benchmark it beats strong guidance baselines on stapled, head-to-tail, disulfide, and bicyclic closures alike.
arxiv-2605-23607: Li studies how disorder affects exotic phases in two-dimensional altermagnetic Josephson junctions, two conventional superconductors joined by a d-wave magnet. Disorder can drive the exotic pi phase into the conventional zero phase, sharply suppressing critical current, through shifts in tunneling Cooper-pair phase and decoherence. The anomalous phi phase proves highly fragile, flipping one-way to either pi or zero phase. Across these transitions the first harmonic of the current-phase relation changes sign, while higher harmonics fade fast, showing disorder's power to tailor junction phases.
arxiv-2605-23707: Dehigama and colleagues propose Flare, a hybrid microservice design mixing virtual machines with serverless functions for load spikes. VM-based setups handle steady load well and cheaply but scale slowly when load spikes, hurting performance. Extra capacity avoids slowdowns but costs more and leaves capacity under-used. Flare uses virtual machines for steady workloads and elastic scaling for spikes, spotting overloaded services and shifting only their excess load to serverless, limiting cost overhead. Flare fits into existing auto-scaling infrastructure with minimal control-plane changes and no app changes.
arxiv-2605-23907: Durif and Nozière describe a flow-tube reactor built from standard tubing for studying gas reactions near room temperature and pressure. Reaction time is set by tube length or by a second arm acting as an exhaust branch, freeing reactor pressure from inlet flows. The design gives a narrow spread of residence times, fast mixing, and low wall reactivity from PFA plastic. Tested on one ozonolysis reaction, it offers a compact, low-cost rival to movable-injector tubes for air chemistry and uptake studies.
arxiv-2605-24107: Li and three co-authors derive the maximum blazar neutrino flux in the one-zone leptohadronic jet model from observed X-ray flux and attainable parameters. Analytical and numerical modelling agree, and both show predicted fluxes do not much exceed earlier one-zone results and stay below IceCube-inferred levels. The one-zone scenario alone therefore looks unlikely to explain high-energy neutrino-blazar associations fully. Multi-zone models or other sites, like the jet base or hot corona, are needed to explain blazar neutrino origins better.
arxiv-2605-24207: Lubarsky and four co-authors bring deep-learning design inside database queries instead of shuttling data outside. Conventional pipelines translate relational data into graphs and run graph neural networks elsewhere, paying overhead for the round trip, yet those networks operate on tuple embeddings shaped by joins. The authors attach provenance to each tuple as a learnable vector embedding, then lift queries to act jointly on data and embeddings. Their RelaNN, built on PyTorch and cuDF, implements graph convolutional, heterogeneous transformer, hypergraph, and homomorphism networks with short programs.
arxiv-2605-24707: Yuan Bian and others argue task tests in depression research should not be analyzed alone. Separate studies miss links and shared latent structure across tasks. Their SHIFT framework models tasks jointly, with latent factors capturing cross-task links and individual differences in choices, response times, and strategy switching. An EM-style variational method dodges heavy integration while preserving time structure. Simulations show gains over single-task studies. Applied to depression, it finds patients engage and focus less versus healthy controls, with shared parameters hinting at treatment-linked patterns.
arxiv-2605-24807: Shayan Jalilian and Abdul Bais build CLIP-Guided SAM, a segmentation framework with meaning built into the image encoder. Promptable models like the Segment Anything Model draw strong masks but stay semantically blind, needing external prompts for categories. Older vision-language methods make spatial prompts for SAM in a separate step. Instead, CLIP-derived text, vision, and similarity features pass through lightweight adapters, letting meaning guide mask prediction. The promptable interface stays intact, and tests show results hinge on train-test prompt consistency.
arxiv-2605-25107: Jules Berman, Tobias Blickhan, and Benjamin Peherstorfer use gauge freedom to learn non-gradient dynamics of stochastic systems. Work focuses on gradient flows from potentials. Among flows, gradient flows minimize kinetic energy. Choosing fields by criteria is gauge freedom, which they exploit. They propose Non-Gradient Flows, inferring non-gradient dynamics through a weak continuity-equation formulation. That allows vector fields and criteria beyond kinetic energy. On low- and high-dimensional physics problems, it improves accuracy over gradient baselines and captures non-potential transport.
arxiv-2605-25207: Shashank Joshi and Wojciech Golab separate reentrancy protection from smart contract logic by moving it into the proxy layer. Reentrancy attacks drained around 80 million dollars from decentralized apps last year. Their Sentinel proxy intercepts every call to the implementation contract. A dual-mode design pairs a gas-optimized internal guard with an external lock registry for cross-contract attacks. On 70 vulnerable contracts it reaches full coverage across four attack categories, beating existing solutions by over 40 percent.
arxiv-2605-25507: Ankur Samanta and colleagues sharpen credit assignment in language-model reasoning training. Verifiable-reward methods now spread one outcome reward evenly over every token, ignoring which steps helped or hurt. Reset methods return to an intermediate state and resample continuations, attributing outcome gaps to the choice made there. Random resets pick states at random, while self-resets let the model locate its own error and restart there. Across models and reasoning benchmarks, the self-reset method beats standard and random-reset training using only the model itself.
arxiv-2605-26007: Floresca and five colleagues test speech-based dementia screening in Filipino and English. No earlier work had tried it in Filipino speech, though switching between the two languages is rife in the Philippines. The team builds a matched set of four thousand transcripts from DementiaBank, with hand-made Filipino versions that keep signs of mental decline. Five model types are tried under same-language training, zero-shot transfer, and joint training. The design splits language effects from task effects and shows where joint training gains most.
arxiv-2605-26207: Sayak Bhattacharjee, Tatia Kiliptari, and Dmitrii Maslov develop a conserving relaxation-time approximation (2026). It projects electron-electron collisions onto the full space of conserved quantities while keeping energy resolution. Unlike cruder versions, it follows states close to, though not exactly at, the Fermi surface, the boundary between filled and empty electron states. Applied to charge transport in Fermi liquids, it reproduces exact limits and scalings, matching exact answers at the percent level for several observables.
arxiv-2605-26607: Zhiyuan Lu offers a faster route to log-linear estimates for dual-system population counts used in census work. Dual-system methods infer how many people each source missed, and log-linear fits via EM steps promise counts for every incomplete group. Yet the arithmetic blows up as populations split by state, ethnicity, and other factors, stalling joint analysis. Lu's alternative reaches the same maximum-likelihood estimates with far less computation, reopening multi-factor census estimation.
arxiv-2605-26707: Sun, Min, and Das prove new upper bounds for the sum of the k largest eigenvalues of symmetric matrices, numbers that capture a matrix's main stretch directions. Applied to graph adjacency matrices, their bounds improve a related result by Mohar. For Laplacian matrices, they show Brouwer's conjecture holds for small k on almost all graphs, a solid step toward settling it fully.
arxiv-2605-26807: Wu and six colleagues build HTMLCure, a framework that tests and repairs language-model-made web pages by actually using them in a browser. The evaluator drives pages across viewports and interaction states, records hard browser evidence, and hands the model keyframes from real runs instead of still screenshots. A repair loop then diagnoses faults, tries fixes, and keeps only quality-cleared pages. The refined set lifts a 27B model to 50.6 on HTMLBench-400 and close to top reference systems on MiniAppBench.
arxiv-2605-27007: Berggren and eight co-authors characterize amply framed directed acyclic graphs whose flow polytopes project onto locally anti-blocking g-polytopes. They describe the minimal faces of the g-polytope holding a fixed pair of vertices. They prove the induced unimodular triangulation is a pulling triangulation and name the pulling orders that yield it. Coherence diagrams, a new counting model, drive the proofs, with possible spin-offs to gentle Nakayama algebras.
arxiv-2605-27307: Mutasim Mim studies triangle families whose edge-triangle incidence matrix has a large spectral gap. He shows a large gap forces strong overlap and high minimum degree, with every edge lying in many triangles. The full triangle set on a clique marks an isolated peak: just above it sits a forbidden interval, and recovery waits for a positive share of the next gap.
arxiv-2605-27407: Hudi He and colleagues benchmark fairness in spiking neural networks across demographic coverage, spurious features, and hardware effects. Models trained on biased data show 23 percent higher false positive rates for underrepresented groups, with edge hardware widening gaps by up to 41 percent. Cloud-built bias fixes often degrade under tight resources, so fairness and hardware efficiency need joint design.
arxiv-2605-27607: Tushar Karnik and colleagues show continuous-wave vacuum squeezing on a chip in thin-film lithium niobate. Their adaptively poled traveling-wave guide reaches about 18 decibels of squeezing and about 20 decibels of anti-squeezing at 1570 nanometers. The result is the highest squeezing reported for any integrated light platform, with clean statistical checks of on-chip performance.
arxiv-2605-28007: Niclas Pokel and Benjamin F. Grewe build networks that reuse parts instead of burying every computation in shared weights. Their Vector Network picks a sparse set of reusable weight atoms per input, composing a custom low-rank matrix for each sample. On compositional benchmarks it matched rivals in distribution and cut out-of-distribution error roughly tenfold on recombined factors.
arxiv-2605-28107: P G Romeo and Riya Jose revisit bundles and chains from category theory, tracing the chain categories that arise from bundle categories. They verify these categories carry subobjects, building on normal categories introduced for regular semigroups. The work ties classical bundle notions, from fibre bundles to principal bundles, into one categorical frame.
arxiv-2605-28207: Kim and colleagues convert mixture-of-experts models into ordinary dense models for memory-tight deployment. Experts are scored, selected, and grouped, then merged into a dense feed-forward network and polished by distillation from the expert teacher. Across hundreds of configurations, diversity-aware scoring won, and expert-to-dense conversion beat dense-to-dense pruning at matched size.
arxiv-2605-28407: Chuanpeng Hou, Huirong Yan, and Siqi Zhao propose imaging weak fields between planets through spectral-line polarization, rather than relying on few in-place probes. They focus on sodium D lines in Mercury's magnetosphere, computing polarization from sunlight from one direction as the field direction shifts it. A three-dimensional forward model then yields synthetic maps of light strength and its signal. The signal maps trace the large-scale field shape, and a 1.8-meter telescope could image it at two-arcsecond resolution in about ten minutes.
arxiv-2605-28507: Torben Berndt and five colleagues extend sequence universality from label tasks to generative time-series work with SLiCEs, structured linear controlled differential equations. They prove that maximally expressive SLiCEs can mimic the path laws of continuous causal pushforwards, making them universal time-series generators. Their SLiCE model applies this theory to flow matching on path space. Greater power improves odds-based forecasts and later tasks while keeping time-based perks, such as handling any grid, even irregular ones.
arxiv-2605-28707: Aisha Aijaz and three colleagues model moral reasoning as a spread over ethical theories rather than a single binary or scalar judgment. They build a normative ethics simplex joining consequentialism, virtue ethics, and deontology, plus fifteen finer subtheories. A two-stream normative-semantic design fuses theory and meaning, and a stacking ensemble learns the best fit on a 450-case benchmark. Tests reach about 89 percent accuracy, and ablation studies show structured ethical reasoning beats bare semantic embeddings.
arxiv-2605-28807: William Overman and Mohsen Bayati introduce Calibrated Collective Oversight, which pools helper scores into a penalty for straying from caution. Shared caution taxes actions by overseer concern. Good actions still win when overseers find them fine, losing only when concern builds. The method tunes this caution live with Conformal Decision Theory, keeping bad outcomes below a user-set target with finite-time bounds. On a tweaked SWE-bench, weaker overseers constrain a hostile rogue agent. On MACHIAVELLI it cuts ethical violations a lot while keeping reward.
arxiv-2605-29007: Xinming Yang and Jun Li build a framework for generating synthetic errors aimed at a five-class Bloom-informed taxonomy. A Generation Agent drafts a candidate wrong solution for a target class, and an Examination Agent judges whether the draft is wrong and class-consistent. The recipe yields class-stratified synthetic error datasets where real student corpora are unavailable. Targeted error generation proves much harder than free-form wrong-answer generation, and answer grounding helps more than extra examples or textbook content.
arxiv-2605-29207: David M. Rothschild and colleagues argue AI's biggest disruption lies ahead, in a third stage called Reconstruction. Most organizations still use AI merely to speed pre-AI workflows, through Augmentation and then Automation. Reconstruction rebuilds workflows and markets around delegation, machine links, continuous monitoring, and auditable constraints. Reaching it takes trust infrastructure, machine-legible data, new workflow design, and incentives favoring rebuilding over local tweaks. Examples span shops, schools, news, and coding, and the future is not predetermined: leaders must steer it toward broad welfare gains.
arxiv-2605-29307: Alireza Salemi and colleagues present GrepSeek, which treats a text corpus as its search environment. Instead of ranked documents from a pre-built index, the agent finds evidence through executable shell commands. Training runs in two stages: the policy is initialized from verified Tutor and Planner trajectories, then refined with Group Relative Policy Optimization. Pruned adaptive command execution and sharded-parallel corpus search preserve equivalence with sequential execution while cutting latency sharply. Across eight open-domain benchmarks, GrepSeek achieves the strongest overall performance.
arxiv-2605-29707: Jianuo Huang and five colleagues split two jobs that speculative decoding usually tangles: mapping causal links among draft tokens and running the draft itself. Their system, Domino, first drafts a whole block in parallel, then polishes it with a light head that adds prefix-based causal detail. A staged training plan first firms up the parallel base, then shifts weight toward the causally fixed final output. On Qwen3 models the scheme ran over five times faster end to end under one backend and near six times the throughput under another.
arxiv-2605-29807: Egor Shevchenko and Elena Bruches compare two ways to catch label errors in Russian training data. Label noise, even in benchmarks, drags down how well models generalize. They test two filters, Confident Learning and Dataset Cartography, across three Russian corpora of varied size, classes, and domain, using a fine-tuned Russian BERT. Filtering helps most on small, noisy sets, where Confident Learning lifts macro F1 markedly, while on large, clean sets it adds little. Targeted removal beats random removal, confirming that both filters find real errors, not smaller data.
arxiv-2605-30107: Songbo Hu and seven colleagues introduce HEALTHDIAL, a large multilingual spoken dialogue dataset for knowledge-grounded information seeking in health. It holds 6000 dialogues, 1500 per language, grounded in trusted World Health Organization content, with 163 hours of speech from native speakers of varied dialects across Arabic, Chinese, English and Spanish. Speakers carry demographic and sociolinguistic annotations. Benchmark tests across dialogue tasks reveal steady performance gaps between languages, even among high-resource ones. The authors publish the dataset, a prototype system, and an evaluation toolkit.
arxiv-2605-30207: Will Jack and three co-authors audit how persona reshapes brand recommendations in retrieval-augmented chat. Adding a persona to a best-CRM prompt drops recommendation similarity by roughly a tenth to a fifth against a baseline. The effect is stratified by prominence: leaders stay resistant, while midmarket brands swap up to three quarters of recommendations as persona changes. The Anthropic model reacts more strongly than OpenAI configurations, consistent with its unattributed route. Brand perception scores therefore depend on the buyer persona behind each query.
arxiv-2605-30307: An-Chieh Cheng and 14 co-authors present GR3D, a spatial vision language model with explicit, implicit and monocular grounding. An implicit mechanism identifies entity mentions during generation and inserts region tokens into the text stream, letting the model cite visual evidence. A monocular 3D design predicts bounding boxes from grounded region queries, with intrinsic-aware normalization and geometric supervision. These capabilities let GR3D decompose spatial problems into 2D perception followed by 3D inference. GR3D improves across grounded and non-grounded benchmarks, showing grounding strengthens spatial understanding.
arxiv-2606-00007:
Johnson designs governance rules for knowledge bases curated jointly by AI agents in this 2026 arXiv paper. Human platforms evolved moderation systems over two decades, but porting them to agents runs into gaps he flags. Agents are stateless, so deterrence-based sanctions lose force. Identical models undermine the variety that makes crowd wisdom work. And sycophancy collapses debate. His curation protocol answers with three layers covering artifact handling, reputation-weighted voting after structured debate, and graduated sanctions adapted for stateless agents.

Simulations with 100 agents drawn from seven archetypes tested the protocol under two adversity scenarios. It traded a little precision in calm conditions for far more strength under attack. Under moderate adversity its precision reached about 0.83 versus 0.79 for majority voting, with the gap widening under stress in their runs. Removing components one at a time showed commit-reveal voting, which hides votes until all are cast, gave the largest improvement.
arxiv-2606-00207:
Burba, Borodinas, and Juzeliūnas map a route to flat bands for super-cold atoms in dark states. Cold atoms can be held in states that shun light. A known link ties a shape-based push to a fake field in such rigs. When the link holds, the ground band turns flat like a Landau level.

The team finds a broad rule for the light fields that makes the link hold. Wave mixes of three, four, or six beams meet the rule. These give a smooth field of one sign, plus thin flux spikes. Drift from the fine tune turns spikes into small flipped patches. That drift and weak light grip each widen the band. Paired right, the two flaws can shrink the width a lot. The band can end near flat, fit for Hall-type tests.
arxiv-2606-00407:
Everson and Ostendorf learn speech tone traits that keep the talker's name out. Tone traits, like pitch and beat, help tools grasp and make speech. Those same traits leak who talks, which raises privacy fears. Their work splits tone wealth from name marks in one learned code.

A self-taught code is built with tricks that pull the two apart. Tests probe the code on three tasks in all. Pitch rebuild is one, and tone event spots fill the rest. The code beats raw tone traits and a HuBERT base on those tasks. Name marks stay well split from the tone code. Tone-based end tasks show no loss from that split.
arxiv-2606-00607:
Sen and Dey build fake three-grade forms from a pair of three-grade quantum units. Such units, called qutrits, hold three states in place of two. Groups of states in the SU(3) frame give a rich base for new forms. Rydberg states are the more known route to such forms.

Nine linked states of SU(3) type form the core of their frame. The pair's push law maps to a fake three-grade space through them. No Rydberg state need be brought in for that map. Link strength in the fake forms is then tracked in time. Two gauges for that link are set in SU(3) terms. One grows a known Wootters-type gauge to the new case.
arxiv-2606-00707:
Kamiyama studies a size-like measure for finite metric spaces in this 2026 maths paper. The measure is called magnitude. When a space is shrunk, its copies collapse to a single point. Yet the magnitude can still record how that collapse took place.

Kamiyama builds a family of cyclic two-chunk spaces, set by four parameters, and works out their magnitude in exact form. With that formula he finds balanced cases whose small-scale magnitude falls below one. One case has twelve points, and its limit is 44/59, well under one. The question grows from Leinster's work on magnitude and from a small-scale view set out by Roff and Yoshinaga. The result shows that a space can look like a point yet keep a rich trace of its shape.
arxiv-2606-01007:
Xu and co-authors place AI experts on chips by task, not by global average, in this 2026 paper. Mixture of experts models switch on a few expert parts per input. In distributed serving, experts talk across GPUs, and routing skews the load. Past placement groups experts that often fire together, from one pooled trace across all tasks.

That pooling erases the real driver, they argue. Expert pairs locked tight in one task family may be strangers in another. Their method, TACG, reads dispatch traces per task family. It scores each expert's taste for each family and reweights the co activation graph so family local links rule. Each expert then takes a primary GPU under strict capacity caps. A companion step copies generic experts, the ones central in all families, to more chips, which guards the static plan against live workload skew.
arxiv-2606-02307:
Kanwal and co-authors generate tests that hunt for failures in robot policy models. Vision-language-action models serve as generalist robot policies. Their evaluation relies largely on static benchmarks. Task scenes are sampled randomly in those benchmarks. In high dimensional embodied spaces, failures are sparse and clustered. Static benchmarking can underestimate robustness risks for that reason.

Evaluation is reframed as an active failure discovery problem. Diversity driven exploration is combined with surrogate models. Those surrogates are learned from observed executions. Testing is steered toward high risk yet diverse scene regions. Four state of the art VLA models are tested. The method uncovers up to 29.7 percent more failures than baselines. More diverse failure modes are revealed as well. For one model, the success rate dropped sharply under the tests.
arxiv-2606-02607:
Turtora Zagardo adds explicit geometry to tabular data synthesis. Synthetic tables support private data sharing and augmentation. Diffusion models learn inter-column relations only implicitly. His model, GATD, computes pairwise angles and lengths from column value differences. Those values enter as both inputs and auxiliary targets. A matched ablation shows supervision, not extra inputs, drives the gains.

The MLP version reaches top benchmark performance with far fewer parameters. It uses 3.5 times fewer on average, and up to 25 times fewer on classification tasks. Across ten datasets, it wins most Shape, Trend, and downstream utility scores. Shape error falls by 27 percent and Trend error by 20 percent. Default loss weights transfer to GNN and Transformer denoisers. Shape improves in 27 of 30 cells there. Explicit relational supervision, the author argues, is a portable inductive bias for tabular diffusion.
arxiv-2606-02907:
Sahoo, Jain, Chadha, and Chaudhary test a popular claim about language model internals. Researchers often probe hidden states with linear classifiers. High probe accuracy is taken as proof that a model keeps distinct modes for distinct kinds of reasoning. The team checks that logic on Qwen3-14B.

They probe three benchmarks for deduction, induction, and abduction. At one layer, probes hit 100 percent accuracy with cleanly separated geometry. But the separation came from format, not reasoning. Once source identity, option count, and response length were removed, accuracy fell to chance. Other checks agreed. Traces showed largely shared reasoning across tasks. Steering tests found no functional link between the geometry and reasoning mode. The authors conclude that probes were reading task format. They urge routine format deconfounding in interpretability work. Without it, neat probe results can mislead readers about what a model computes.
arxiv-2606-03107:
Oke and Kant work on safe online learning for control of nonlinear systems. Online approximate dynamic programming needs rich probing signals to learn. But strong probing can push a system past the zone where its local linear model holds. The team studies second-order nonlinear systems and builds a frame that keeps the state in a set safe zone.

Exploration is watched by impulses. When the state nears the edge of the zone, a sharp braking impulse resets it to the inside. Learning then pauses and restarts once the state is back. The full setup is cast as a hybrid system. The authors prove the safe set stays invariant under this scheme, while any probing strength is allowed for critic learning. The state stayed in the valid zone under high-amplitude probing. The learned weights settled to the values given by the algebraic Riccati equation.
arxiv-2606-03207:
Yu and co-authors stabilize the pulse rate of a mode-locked fiber laser with no active feedback. The rate drifts when the cavity length drifts. Their method places an electro-optic modulator in a phase-biased nonlinear amplifying loop mirror. Cross-phase modulation between electrical and optical pulses in the crystal does the work.

That coupling shifts the spectrum in a way that offsets cavity drift through group velocity dispersion. The capture range reaches 2.3 millimeters, far past what index change alone gives. The lock held tight for 11 hours. Its spread was as low as 9 microhertz at a one-second sample time. That is a fractional instability near four parts in ten trillion. The team also shows dynamic optical sampling by rate tuning, with a fast refresh and a scan range over 305 picoseconds.
arxiv-2606-03307:
Jin and co-authors add hyperbolic retrieval to graph foundation models. Such models pretrain on graphs at scale for cross-domain use. Their stored knowledge still fails under distribution shift. Retrieval-augmented generation can add outside knowledge at run time. But Euclidean retrieval has a geometric flaw: its volume growth is polynomial, while knowledge bases grow like trees.

The mismatch blurs fine detail in retrieval and breeds a hubness problem. Their framework, HyRAG, indexes the knowledge base in hyperbolic space, which fits tree shape. A retrieval module then fetches knowledge at two grains: broad anchors and local nuance. A dual-path fusion module merges the finds at feature and structure levels. Tests on many graph benchmarks show clear gains in the zero-shot setting. The authors present HyRAG as a way to make graph foundation models generalize with more grace.
arxiv-2606-04107:
Zheng-Hui Huang, Zhixiang Wang, Yu-Lun Liu, and Yung-Yu Chuang present a diffusion model in 2026 that splits a photo into two parts. One part is the scene behind glass. The other is the glare on the glass itself.

Earlier methods forced a hard split in one shot, which often failed when the two layers mixed. Their model instead works in rounds. At each round it rebuilds the two images from a shared internal state, then polishes the result. Trials on synthetic and real photos beat prior methods on clarity and on how sharp the edges look. The approach also handled paired captures, where a second shot helps tell the layers apart.
arxiv-2606-04207:
Lukas D'Angelo and colleagues describe in 2026 a real-time testbed that combines wideband radio identification with wireless power transfer, letting batteryless tags both communicate and harvest energy from the same signals. Their rig is an eight-by-eight distributed antenna system running in a common Wi-Fi band.

The testbed excites a backscatter device, a tag that answers by reflecting signals, and reads its reply within two milliseconds of airtime. Channel estimates then serve two applications at once: steering energy toward the tag and locating it indoors in real time. Energy harvesting gains reached up to twelve decibels over unfocused transmission. The authors present the platform as shared infrastructure for experimenting with joint communication, powering, and positioning.
arxiv-2606-04307:
Jun Hu proposes Folded Transport MCMC in 2026, a sampling method that eliminates the label-switching headache in Bayesian mixture models. Because mixture components are interchangeable, the posterior has a factorial number of identical modes, and standard samplers either hop poorly between them or need after-the-fact relabeling.

His sampler restricts the chain to a fundamental domain, a sorted slice of the space holding exactly one copy of each symmetric mode. Proposals come from a learned flow whose density is symmetrized over the label permutations, so the target stays correct on the reduced space. A computable convergence diagnostic comes along, and it sharpens when folding is applied. Across mixture tests and real accelerometer data from a supertall building, improvements ranged from twofold to over a hundredfold.
arxiv-2606-04507:
Zhu and colleagues train AI research assistants whose grader improves alongside the writer, in a 2026 arXiv paper on deep research systems. Producing a research report has no single ground-truth answer. Existing work uses a language model as judge with fixed rubrics. But a static evaluator cannot raise its standards as the solver improves. Optimization pressure then saturates. Their framework, SCORE, couples evaluator and solver in one shared-parameter model. Both improve together.

A meta-harness steers the process. It adjusts the evaluation environment to solver performance. It encourages valid evaluation dimensions and deeper evaluator search. Across deep research benchmarks, SCORE produced consistent improvements in report quality. The authors present co-evolving evaluation and generation as a promising direction. It suits research agents whose outputs cannot be checked against an answer key.
arxiv-2606-04607:
Sevilla and colleagues demonstrate a microscope technique that finds nanoscale defects buried inside silicon carbide wafers without damaging them, in a 2026 arXiv paper. They leave no resolvable surface marks. Standard photoluminescence contrast is quenched by background doping.

The combination yields high-contrast, high-resolution images of dislocations below the surface. So the method identifies as well as locates. The authors describe the approach as simple and tolerant of surface imperfections. It offers a practical route toward industrial in-line inspection of SiC substrates. SiC is central to power electronics. Catching buried defects before device fabrication saves costly failures.
arxiv-2606-04707:
Zhang, Yang, and Jin recalculate how much of the dark matter could be light primordial black holes, paying attention to a modeling choice others glossed over, in a 2026 arXiv cosmology paper. Standard Hawking evaporation disfavors such black holes, but the memory-burden effect can extend their lifetimes by suppressing emission after about half the mass is lost. Earlier cosmological studies modeled the switch into the burden phase as instantaneous. This paper treats the crossover as continuous, comparing additive and multiplicative ways of combining the two evaporation rates through a smoothed profile.

The additive crossover always yields weaker bounds than the multiplicative one, while both are tighter than the instantaneous transition. In the mass range studied, the additive case can allow black holes to be about a tenth of dark matter where the multiplicative case allows only a hundredth. Specifying the combination rule, they conclude, is essential for honest constraints.
arxiv-2606-04807:
Reddy, Yang, and Zhai adapt a reinforcement learning method to the messy job of reducing social bias in language models, in a 2026 arXiv paper. Unlike verifiable tasks, bias has no single ground truth, so rewards are high-variance. Direct Preference Optimization is limited by its offline nature and lack of exploration, while Proximal Policy Optimization can destabilize. Their framework, BiasGRPO, uses group-relative policy optimization, normalizing rewards across a group of sampled completions instead of trusting a learned value function.

Substituting the group-relative baseline reduces instability while keeping the exploration benefits of online training. BiasGRPO outperforms both DPO and PPO across multiple benchmarks. To run it, the authors extend a bias dataset across domains and contexts, and they build and release a custom bias reward model that guides generation without degrading the model's knowledge.
arxiv-2606-05107:
Elouan Gardès and co-authors propose FINO in this 2026 arXiv paper, a label-free way to adapt vision foundation models to specialized scientific domains. Generic vision models degrade on fields like microscopy or Earth observation. The usual fix, supervised fine-tuning, struggles there: labels are scarce, and narrow training can collapse the model's generality. Scientific datasets, however, come with rich metadata that standard pipelines ignore.

FINO adapts representations in a self-supervised way guided by that metadata, handling both discrete labels and continuous values. Its objective encourages the representation to preserve informative factors while suppressing spurious ones, such as sensor or batch effects. Across fluorescence microscopy, Earth observation, wildlife monitoring, and medical imaging, FINO outperformed unsupervised domain adaptation. It even beat fully supervised adaptation. It also exceeded specialized domain systems while using no task labels for the backbone and only lightweight probes on top.
arxiv-2606-05207:
Absos Ali Shaikh and Kamiruzzaman examine pseudosymmetry, Ricci solitons, and curvature inheritance in Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker spacetime in this 2026 arXiv paper. This cosmos is the standard model of a homogeneous, isotropic cosmos, yet its geometry had never had a full curvature examination.

They show it meets a pseudosymmetric-type curvature condition and several related ones on the conformal and conharmonic tensors. Certain Tachibana tensors built from those curvatures depend linearly on a symmetrized combination. It is also a 2-quasi-Einstein manifold of Roter type. Its Ricci tensor is neither cyclic parallel nor of Codazzi type, though it meets several compatibility needs. Studying solitons and inheritance symmetries, they find almost Ricci soliton and eta-Ricci Yamabe soliton forms for the time and radial fields but not the angular one. They close by setting it beside the inhomogeneous Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi spacetime.
arxiv-2606-05307:
Noemi La Bella and colleagues ask how faint a jet base the Event Horizon Telescope can detect around the black hole M87-star in this 2026 arXiv paper. M87 hosts a famous relativistic jet, but spotting jet emission right at horizon scales, next to the bright accretion flow, is hard.

They generated observations for three array configurations, the 2021 and 2022 campaigns plus a near-future one, using semi-analytic accretion-jet models whose jet brightness can be tuned. Jet detectability depended strongly on intensity, array configuration, and imaging method, and the 2022 array's improved short-baseline coverage was a significant step up. The authors conclude the telescope is sensitive to weak horizon-scale jet emission. If post-2021 images show no jet signature, the inner jet must contribute only a small part of the compact flux.
arxiv-2606-05407:
Haofei Lu and colleagues present MoDex in this 2026 arXiv paper, a diffusion policy for sequentially grasping several objects with one dexterous hand without putting any of them down. Most dexterous grasping methods commit the hand's degrees of freedom to a single object, wasting its dexterity and leaving nothing in reserve for the next grasp.

The policy predicts the next gripper pose from observations, conditioned on a point cloud and on an opposition space, a specification of which fingers participate in the current grasp. Training proceeds in two stages: imitation learning on expert demonstrations, then reinforcement learning fine-tuning. That improves success rates over the pretrained policy and eases simulation-to-real transfer. Evaluated on a Franka Panda arm with an Allegro Hand in MuJoCo simulation and on real hardware, MoDex beat the learning-based baselines. The margins were 3 to 18 percentage points in both settings.
arxiv-2606-05907:
Okabe and Komatsu bend a document collection into a curved map where distance means meaning in a 2026 arXiv paper. Their knowledge manifold starts from character-level word-piece frequency vectors for each paper. A constrained layout places papers on a two-dimensional surface, close when semantically near. Smoothed particle interpolation then estimates the knowledge profile at any point on the map, even empty spots.

Directional gradients show how topics shift across the surface. A Gaussian process layer adds uncertainty estimates and each paper's contribution at a query point. Shortest paths on the curved surface, its geodesics, trace how one research area morphs into another. The test corpus held twenty papers on fiber-reinforced composites and aerospace structures. The map recovered meaningful research clusters without being told the groupings. Geodesic paths likewise followed sensible topic transitions. The framework offers analysts a geometry for literature, not just a list.
arxiv-2606-06007:
Haoyang Cao, Chen, Han, and Xu build diffusion models that generate time series without peeking at the future in a 2026 arXiv paper. Synthetic sequential data serves finance, healthcare, energy, and operations, but naive diffusion extensions scramble time dependence. Worse, they can leak future information into earlier steps, which real forecasting forbids. The sequential forward-backward framework adds and removes noise along the sequence itself. Each step conditions on the history built so far, enforcing adaptedness.

A new score-matching objective keeps training efficient and parallel. The theory delivers guarantees in layers: score approximation, score estimation, then distribution fit, with ReLU networks as the worked example. Synthetic tests on ARMA models and Gaussian processes confirmed the approach. A finance demo built mean-variance optimal portfolios from generated data. Code is public. Adaptedness, the authors argue, is not a detail but the defining constraint for honest sequential generation.
arxiv-2606-06107:
Clason and colleagues run quantum key distribution across three hundred kilometers of Swedish fiber in a 2026 arXiv paper. QKD promises information-theoretic secrecy, but deployment faces distance, mixed infrastructure, and classical traffic sharing the glass. The link joins Linköping University to the Stockholm hub of Sweden's national quantum infrastructure. Two hundred seventy kilometers of deployed single-mode fiber form the backbone.

A thirty-three-kilometer multi-core fiber segment stands in for a metropolitan access link, bringing the total past three hundred kilometers. Commercial QKD systems pair with superconducting nanowire detectors to survive the loss. The team switched the quantum channel between cores while Ethernet traffic and injected noise ran alongside. Keys generated en route protected an image transmission with one-time-pad encryption. Image fidelity hinged on the key budget and compression choice. The demonstration targets hybrid quantum-classical networks as they will be built.
arxiv-2606-06207:
Yukiko Kawakami and colleagues hunt for hidden toxicity patterns in Japanese animal drug reports in this 2026 arXiv paper. Pharmacovigilance means watching for harmful drug effects after medicines reach real use. Japan's reporting rules and the differing biology of each species can hide patterns that pooled data would blur. Instead of training a predictor, the team looks for structure directly, in a way regulators can inspect.

They encoded more than four thousand high confidence adverse event reports, covering nine thousand eighty drug and event combinations, by organ system and adjusted for species reporting bias. Clustering found three clear species patterns: liver dominant effects in companion animals, kidney toxicity in ruminants, and skin sensitivity in sheep. Drug clusters matched known pharmacological classes in eighty three percent of cases, and cosine similarity beat rival measures at grouping the sparse reports.
arxiv-2606-06307:
Mohammad Taha Shah and Mohamed-Slim Alouini model networks of stratospheric aircraft in this 2026 arXiv paper on future communications. High altitude platforms circle between twenty and fifty kilometers up, promising broadband for rural, maritime, and island communities. Fleets of them will patrol in rings, so coverage and interference depend on the patrol geometry itself. Standard network analysis tools assume platforms scattered at random, which misses that structure.

They build a stochastic geometry framework on the spherical Earth, with two ring based point processes for patrol fleets. One scatters platforms randomly along each ring; the other fixes the count per ring. They derive coverage formulas and fold in the propulsion cost of circular flight. Under the random model, patrol radius creates clear optima for coverage and energy use. Under the fixed fleet model, performance barely responds to radius once fleet size is set.
arxiv-2606-06507:
Yu Zhong and Luyao Li model a stroke relevant artery with flexible curves in this 2026 arXiv paper on medical geometry. The cervical segment of the internal carotid artery twists in ways that matter for stroke diagnosis and surgical planning, and its centerline must be fitted accurately from scans. Ordinary polynomial fits oscillate, overfit, and force users to hand pick the polynomial order. The authors fit with fractional polynomials instead, allowing non integer powers that bend more naturally.

Choosing the order is automated with the Bayesian Information Criterion. Their effective order idea prunes candidate orders using sample statistics, shrinking the search space. On three hundred seventy nine clinical cases, the method beat traditional integer order fitting in accuracy and noise robustness, staying stable across four noise levels. Computation fell sharply too, from about one hundred fifty three seconds to about twenty three.
arxiv-2606-06607:
Yara do Amaral Coutinho and co-authors hunt a two particle dark sector at the Large Hadron Collider in this 2026 arXiv paper. Their theory has two neutral massive vector particles, both odd under a dark parity symmetry. The lighter is stable and a dark matter candidate. The heavier can decay by emitting a photon. When a collider produces the pair alongside ordinary quark jets, the signature is striking: one photon, jets, and missing momentum carried off by the invisible dark particles.

The team compares two search strategies: a single inclusive selection on missing momentum, and a three bin strategy keeping some shape information. The binned analysis improves the expected reach substantially. It probes regions where freeze out yields exactly the observed dark matter abundance. The authors also discuss a freeze in alternative, and warn their effective theory loses reliability at high masses.
arxiv-2606-06807:
A set function assigns a number to every group in a collection, and an additive one gives each union exactly the sum of its parts. Ho and Kania study functions that are only nearly additive in this 2026 arXiv paper. The Kalton-Roberts theorem promises that any such function sits within a fixed multiple of its error of a truly additive one, and the smallest such multiple is a famous unknown constant.

The original bound was forty four point five, later trimmed to thirty eight point eight. Ho and Kania now prove about nineteen point eight four, more than halving the original. Their proof changes which collections feed a recombination step built on expander graphs. Exact rational arithmetic checks every step, and the proof is formalized in Lean.
arxiv-2606-07007:
Sparse autoencoders promise to name what each neuron in a network has learned. Zhang, Lin, and Lee give that promise a mathematical spine in this 2026 arXiv paper. A concept, they propose, is simply a set of data points. Learning a concept means aligning the model's induced set with the human one.

Three grades of success follow. A neuron may merely detect a concept, separate it cleanly, or approximate it closely. Each grade yields geometric conditions and error bounds. Capacity limits say when one neuron suffices and when teams are needed. The framework explains familiar quirks of these models. Features split, get absorbed, form families, and stack into hierarchies. Formal concept analysis links the two directions of interpretation, which need not agree. Experiments on synthetic data with two autoencoder styles illustrate the theory in action.
arxiv-2606-07307:
Guo and Gordon study how a swirling flow can move the threshold for thermal explosion in this 2026 arXiv paper. The setting is the classic Frank-Kamenetskii model of combustion, where heat from a chemical reaction competes with cooling at a vessel's walls. One parameter controls the balance: below a critical value a steady temperature profile exists; above it, no steady state remains and explosion follows. The authors add a regular vortical flow, meaning a circulating motion inside the vessel.

They prove that when the reaction term grows fast enough, a suitable vortex can reverse the direction in which the threshold shifts. The striking exception is a disk-shaped vessel, where the trick fails. The paper describes the extremal solutions, the borderline profiles exactly at the threshold. Those profiles are always classical: smooth genuine solutions rather than weak limiting objects, a point the authors establish in detail.
arxiv-2606-07407:
Ju and Kim ask how few structured blocks are needed to build an arbitrary matrix, in this 2026 arXiv paper. A Toeplitz matrix is constant along each diagonal, giving it a description. Results say a matrix factors into a product of Toeplitz matrices, but the minimal count depends on the matrix and the structure allowed. The authors generalize the question to families of matrices forming an algebraic variety, a set defined by polynomial equations.

They define factorization varieties capturing products of a number of factors, and a border form based on limits of products. The authors compute dimensions of these varieties for Toeplitz, Hankel, bidiagonal, tridiagonal, skew-symmetric, and companion structures. For lower bounds on length they develop a method based on displacement rank, a measure of near-structure, which yields equations defining them. Upper bounds come from alternating minimization. Geometry provides evidence on the varieties' degrees in an example.
arxiv-2606-07507:
Sabando-Alvarez and Precup write down polynomial equations for the pieces of geometric spaces central to representation theory, in this 2026 arXiv paper. Springer fibers are varieties inside the flag variety, the space of nested chains, attached to nilpotent matrices. For matrices with two Jordan blocks, the fiber's irreducible components correspond both to two-row Young tableaux and to noncrossing matchings. Inspired by work on matrix Schubert varieties, the authors define an explicit polynomial ideal for each noncrossing matching.

They prove those ideals define the components, leaning on descriptions from earlier authors. Examples computed with the ideals then suggest two guessed formulas for each component's cohomology class, an algebraic marker used in Schubert calculus. The authors prove both conjectures for one family of tableaux using algebra methods. Turning abstract pieces into concrete equations makes once-hidden invariants computable, at least across the two-row landscape the paper maps.
arxiv-2606-07607:
Zhou, Huang, and Li accuse genomics of validating its methods with cherry-picked anecdotes, in this 2026 arXiv position paper. Deep learning models predict from DNA, and biologists ask them to explain the mechanisms through interpretable machine learning. The field's habit is to apply one method and publish successes. Benchmarking on transcription factor binding, the authors show 3 risks. Different methods give contradictory accounts for the same prediction. Methods fail to locate regulatory motifs, and explanations fail to reflect the model's internal process.

Their remedy borrows clinical trial culture: strict design, consistency and faithfulness checks, biological validity standards, and reporting failures like adverse events. A tiered framework grades genomic methods by evidence strength. Plausible-looking explanations are worse than none when they misdirect lab work. Genomics, they contend, must move from plausibility to validation before its models can guide laboratory work.
arxiv-2606-08307:
Amal Alqahtani, Salama, and Diab examine how mental health is discussed in Arabic-language online communities in this 2026 arXiv paper. Research in this area has centered mostly on English speakers, leaving Arabic discourse little examined. The authors study more than eight thousand posts on the platform X from over six hundred users, identified by a classifier as likely writing from lived experience. The posts come from three communities devoted to borderline personality disorder (BPD), bipolar disorder, and ADHD.

Using a cultural keyword framework, the team characterizes each community's language patterns. In their corpus, bipolar posts used more religious and medical words. BPD posts leaned toward relational, identity, and emotional-distress words. ADHD posts focused more often on practical symptoms and medication. The authors stress the corpus is imbalanced, so the patterns generate hypotheses rather than confirm them.
arxiv-2606-08407:
El-Yaagoubi, Moo Chung, and Ombao build a framework for mapping directed information flow in brain networks, in this 2026 arXiv paper. Neural circuits are full of recurrent feedback loops, which makes characterizing who influences whom difficult. Many existing tools assume a directed acyclic graph, a network without cycles, and therefore cannot represent the loops that real brains contain. The authors' nonparametric, information-theoretic framework is designed to keep those loops visible instead of assuming them away.

The method couples the discrete Hodge decomposition, a way of splitting flows on a network into independent components, with lead-lag mutual information, which detects which signals precede others. The edge flow separates into three orthogonal parts: a gradient term, a curl term isolating feedback loops, and a harmonic term for cyclic flow. A testing layer then identifies nodes whose flow signatures change between conditions.
arxiv-2606-08607:
